title: Cycle Affinity And Winding Localize Eigenvalues Of Markov Generators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky, Naruo Ohga, Sosuke Ito
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. Here we show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector ``winding number'' of some nonequilibrium cycle. In unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number coincides with the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl--Seifert ellipse conjecture.
tldr: This paper proves that complex eigenvalues of Markov generators are localized by nonequilibrium cycles, establishing a tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay.
motivation: To understand how nonequilibrium driving affects the oscillatory relaxation and autocorrelation properties of Markov processes, and to unify previous bounds on eigenvalues.
method: The authors use cycle decomposition and winding numbers to derive geometric bounds on eigenvalues, and prove the Uhl–Seifert ellipse conjecture for multicyclic systems.
result: Each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by cycle affinity and eigenvector winding number; in unicyclic systems, winding number equals eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds.
conclusion: The results reveal fundamental constraints on relaxation timescales in driven systems, with implications for thermodynamic cost of oscillations and design of nonequilibrium processes.

title: Hopper: A Hop-by-hop Entanglement Distribution Protocol For Asynchronous Quantum Networks
authors: Claudio Cicconetti
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum Internet relies on the ability to distribute entangled quantum bits (ebits) between quantum memories at the end nodes, to perform applications like blind or distributed quantum computing that are impossible if end nodes are connected via a classical, i.e., non-quantum network. This need creates new challenges due to the fragile nature of entanglement, which decoheres over short timescales and cannot be amplified, buffered, or retransmitted. Two broad categories of approaches have been proposed in the scientific literature to realize such an entanglement distribution in a given path: one relying on a synchronous time-slotted model, and another one where intermediate nodes interact asynchronously. However, both of them implicitly assume a serial operation, where one ebit is established and made available to the application on end nodes before creating a new one. This is inefficient in long-range networks, with high transmission latencies, if the intermediate nodes have multiple memory qubits that could be used in parallel. To overcome this limitation, in this paper, we study the implications of multiplexing concurrent ebit requests on the same quantum, for both synchronous and asynchronous operation. Furthermore, for the latter, we define a novel distribution protocol, called HOPPER, where the intermediate nodes make autonomous and hop-by-hop decisions on the use of their local resources when establishing an ebit. With numerical simulations, we show that HOPPER is effective in handling multiple ebit requests in parallel, and it exhibits significantly better performance than a synchronous alternative in different scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes HOPPER, a hop-by-hop entanglement distribution protocol for asynchronous quantum networks that supports multiplexing multiple ebit requests in parallel, outperforming synchronous alternatives.
motivation: Existing entanglement distribution protocols assume serial ebit creation, which is inefficient for long-range networks with high latency and multiple memory qubits. The paper aims to improve throughput by multiplexing concurrent ebit requests.
method: The authors define a novel asynchronous protocol (HOPPER) where intermediate nodes make autonomous hop-by-hop decisions to allocate local resources for multiple ebit requests. They compare it with a synchronous time-slotted model via numerical simulations.
result: HOPPER effectively handles multiple parallel ebit requests and shows significantly better performance than synchronous alternatives in various scenarios, especially under high latency and limited resources.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the benefits of asynchronous, multiplexed entanglement distribution for quantum networks, paving the way for more efficient quantum Internet protocols. Future work may explore integration with other quantum network layers.

title: Quantum Meets Statistical-Physical Secrecy: A Novel Hybrid Key Distribution Architecture
authors: Ertugrul Basar
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter proposes a novel hybrid key distribution architecture that jointly exploits quantum key distribution (QKD) and Kirchhoff-law-Johnson-noise (KLJN) statistical-physical key exchange. In the proposed system, an optical BB84-type QKD link operates in coordination with a parallel wired KLJN link, which is used for secure basis handling and, in selected protocols, additional raw key generation. Three novel KLJN-assisted QKD protocols are introduced to eliminate public basis disclosure messages and bit sifting, extract basis-derived key bits, or generate raw key bits under ideal KLJN assumptions. Analytical expressions for the normalized key rate and absolute throughput are derived by accounting for optical channel penalties, KLJN bandwidth constraints, and synchronization bottlenecks. Numerical results show that the proposed hybrid architecture can improve key generation efficiency and throughput in short-haul infrastructures, including metropolitan area networks (MANs) and data center interconnects.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid key distribution architecture combining QKD and KLJN statistical-physical key exchange to eliminate public basis disclosure and improve key rate.
motivation: To overcome the efficiency and security limitations of standalone QKD by integrating a parallel KLJN link for secure basis handling and additional key generation.
method: Designs three KLJN-assisted QKD protocols that use the wired KLJN channel to convey basis information and generate extra raw key bits, with analytical modeling of key rate and throughput.
result: The hybrid architecture improves key generation efficiency and throughput in short-haul networks, with numerical results showing gains in metropolitan area networks and data center interconnects.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable path to enhance QKD performance using statistical-physical methods, though practical implementation challenges remain.

title: Energy-space Quantum Walks: Thermalization Without State Convergence
authors: Renato Moreira Angelo Alana Spak Dos Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce energy-space quantum walks as a minimal framework to investigate equilibration, thermalization, and irreversibility from an effective-dynamics perspective. By mapping the configuration space of a walk onto a ladder of energy eigenlevels, we reinterpret thermalization as transport in energy space, independently of microscopic system--bath details. At the classical level, the resulting birth--death--lazy dynamics leads to equilibration of the energy distribution and, under suitable conditions, to a Gibbs stationary state. We then embed this dynamics into a unitary, collision-assisted model in which coherence is controlled by a single parameter. A central result is a structural decoupling between population dynamics and coherence generation: while the populations evolve according to the classical process and relax to the Gibbs distribution, the full quantum state exhibits a persistent coherence-induced deviation from the thermal manifold. This establishes a minimal scenario of thermalization without state convergence, where equilibration occurs at the level of populations but not at the level of the full density operator. We quantify this effect using the thermal distance to the Gibbs state and derive perturbative bounds that relate the long-time deviation to classical transport properties. Our results show that coherence acts as a controllable and quantitatively bounded source of nonthermal behavior, providing a clear separation between classical equilibration and genuinely quantum corrections.
tldr: This paper introduces energy-space quantum walks as a minimal model for thermalization, showing that populations equilibrate to Gibbs while coherence persists, leading to thermalization without full state convergence.
motivation: To understand equilibration and thermalization from a minimal effective-dynamics perspective, independent of microscopic system-bath details, and to clarify the role of coherence in quantum thermalization.
method: Maps the configuration space of a quantum walk onto energy eigenlevels, uses a birth-death-lazy classical process for population dynamics, and embeds it into a unitary collision model with a single coherence parameter.
result: Populations relax to Gibbs distribution via classical process, but the full quantum state deviates due to coherence; thermal distance to Gibbs state is bounded and controlled by coherence parameter.
conclusion: Provides a clear separation between classical equilibration and quantum corrections, with implications for understanding irreversibility and energy consumption in quantum information processes.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Separable Squeezed States In Finite Memory Structured Reservoir
authors: Ting Yu Austen Couvertier
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement in continuous-variable Gaussian systems is a key resource, and common reservoirs can both suppress and generate correlations. Existing work focused on pre-entangled states or Markovian baths, leaving open whether separable squeezed inputs entangle in structured environments or under modulation. We study two bosonic modes coupled to a common reservoir, each initialized in a separable squeezed vacuum. Dynamics are analyzed utilizing Gaussian covariance methods, evolved under approximate Non-Markovian quantum state diffusion (QSD), finite-temperature pseudomode embeddings, and Bures-based non-Markovian diagnostics. We identify three mechanisms absent in Markovian dynamics: (1) A detuning condition that freezes entanglement trajectories across reservoir correlation times; (2) birth, death, and revival of entanglement from orthogonal inputs; and (3) integer-locked beating with square-wave oscillations produced by periodic detuning. All mechanisms persist at finite temperature, with deviations bounded within 5% in cryogenic regimes and 20% at moderate occupations. These deviation bounds align with cryogenic cavity, phononic, and optomechanical platforms, where structured spectral densities and detuning modulation are already accessible. Structured reservoirs are shown to emerge as tunable entanglement resources for continuous-variable quantum technologies.
tldr: This paper shows that separable squeezed states can become entangled via a common structured reservoir, with novel non-Markovian effects like entanglement freezing, revivals, and integer-locked beating.
motivation: Previous work focused on pre-entangled states or Markovian baths; it was unclear whether separable squeezed inputs could entangle in structured environments or under modulation.
method: The authors use Gaussian covariance methods, approximate Non-Markovian quantum state diffusion (QSD), finite-temperature pseudomode embeddings, and Bures-based non-Markovian diagnostics.
result: They identify three non-Markovian mechanisms: detuning-induced entanglement freezing, birth-death-revival cycles from orthogonal inputs, and integer-locked square-wave oscillations from periodic detuning. These persist at finite temperature with deviations <5% in cryogenic regimes.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs can serve as tunable entanglement resources for continuous-variable quantum technologies, with implications for quantum repeaters and network configurations.

authors: Zahra Baghali Khanian Shokoufe Faraji

Equivalently, for [MATH], this formulation can be expressed in terms of a constrained maximal output Schatten [MATH]-norm. More precisely, for a completely positive map [MATH], we consider the quantity [MATH] defined by optimizing [MATH] over all bipartite states [MATH] whose [MATH]-marginal is maximally mixed. We then establish a general multiplicativity criterion: whenever a completely positive map [MATH] satisfies [MATH] for some constants [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint of [MATH], the quantity [MATH] is multiplicative under tensor powers. Examples of channels satisfying this criterion include the transpose-depolarizing channel, the depolarizing channel, and their respective complementary channels. Furthermore, we show that, for every completely positive map [MATH], multiplicativity of [MATH] implies multiplicativity for its complementary map. motivation: Entanglement of purification is a key measure in quantum information theory, but its additivity properties are not fully understood. This work aims to establish additivity for Rényi-2 version, which is relevant for entanglement distillation and quantum communication.
method: The authors reformulate the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification as a constrained minimum output Rényi entropy problem and express it via maximal output Schatten 2-norm. They then derive a multiplicativity criterion for completely positive maps and apply it to specific channels like the transpose-depolarizing and depolarizing channels.
result: They compute the quantity for the transpose-depolarizing channel and prove multiplicativity under tensor powers. They establish a general criterion based on the Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint and show that multiplicativity for a map implies multiplicativity for its complementary map, leading to additivity for the associated Rényi-2 entanglement of purification.
conclusion: The results provide new additivity results for entanglement of purification, which may have implications for quantum communication protocols and resource theories. Future work could extend to other Rényi indices or more general channels.

title: Interface Piezoelectric Loss In Superconducting Qubits
authors: Haoxin Zhou, Kangdi Yu, Yashwanth Balaji, Sanjit Shirol, Leo Sementilli, Zi-Huai Zhang, Adam Schwartzberg, Alp Sipahigil
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissipation remains a central obstacle to improving superconducting quantum circuits, yet the microscopic origins of loss in widely used materials platforms are not fully understood. Here, we report the observation of interface piezoelectricity-induced dissipation in superconducting qubits fabricated on high-resistivity silicon. Our devices use a transmon qubit with a shunt capacitor that simultaneously serves as an interdigital transducer embedded in a surface acoustic wave resonator. By tuning the qubit transition into resonance with discrete mechanical modes, we observe up to a factor-of-two reduction in qubit lifetime, consistent with energy exchange between the qubit and mechanical modes mediated by piezoelectric coupling at the aluminum-silicon interface. Our findings provide direct evidence for interface piezoelectricity as a distinct loss channel in superconducting qubits. Combined with multiphysics simulations, these findings suggest that interface piezoelectric loss can dominate over loss from two-level systems at sufficiently high frequencies.
tldr: This paper identifies interface piezoelectricity as a new loss channel in superconducting qubits, mediated by coupling to surface acoustic wave modes.
motivation: Understanding microscopic loss mechanisms is crucial for improving superconducting qubit coherence. The authors suspected that piezoelectric coupling at interfaces could cause dissipation, especially at higher frequencies.
method: They fabricated transmon qubits with shunt capacitors acting as interdigital transducers on high-resistivity silicon, forming a surface acoustic wave resonator. By tuning the qubit frequency into resonance with mechanical modes, they measured qubit lifetime changes.
result: They observed up to a factor-of-two reduction in qubit lifetime when the qubit was resonant with mechanical modes, consistent with energy exchange via piezoelectric coupling. Multiphysics simulations suggest this loss can dominate over two-level system loss at high frequencies.
conclusion: Interface piezoelectricity is a distinct and potentially dominant loss channel in superconducting qubits, especially at higher frequencies, and must be considered in qubit design.

title: Wave Packet Landscape In Linear Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kang Xu, Miao-Miao Yi, Zi-Hong Yan, C. P. Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quantum landscape approach to characterize the long-time behavior of wave packet spreading in linear open quantum systems. Instead of treating diffusion, localization, and collapse of the wave packet as separate dynamical phenomena, we show that they originate from the symmetry structure of an underlying landscape in covariance space. The geometry of this landscape determines these distinct long time behaviors. Trapping potentials and bath fluctuations act as distinct symmetry-breaking perturbations, leading to noncommuting long-time limits and abrupt changes in the asymptotic wave-packet width. This geometric picture provides a unified origin for wave-packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in dissipative quantum dynamics.
tldr: A geometric landscape in covariance space unifies wave packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in linear open quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for understanding distinct long-time behaviors of wave packets in dissipative quantum dynamics, which are typically treated separately.
method: Develops a quantum landscape approach based on the symmetry structure of covariance space, analyzing symmetry-breaking perturbations from trapping potentials and bath fluctuations.
result: The geometry of the landscape determines whether the wave packet diffuses, localizes, or collapses; noncommuting limits lead to abrupt changes in asymptotic width.
conclusion: Offers a geometric picture that unifies these phenomena, with implications for understanding decoherence and control in open quantum systems.

title: Quantum Compressed Sensing
authors: Jianyong Hu, Wei Li, Shuxiao Wu, Liwen Zhang, Yongchuang Sun, Jiazhao Tian, Guosheng Feng, Zhixing Qiao, Jianqiang Liu, Changgang Yang, Ruiyun Chen, Chengbing Qin, Guofeng Zhang, Liantuan Xiao, Suotang Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How many measurements are fundamentally required to capture a signal. Shannon's information theory established the bedrock of this question in 1948, the Nyquist Shannon theorem set the first answer, and compressed sensing (CS) rewrote it in 2006 by reducing the required measurement number to M = O(Klog(N/K)) for a K sparse signal. Here, we propose quantum compressed sensing (QCS), a paradigm that reframes signal acquisition as a unitary quantum evolution. By encoding high dimensional signal information into a single quantum probe state, then introducing domain-alignment evolution,a physically realizable unitary transformation that maps the sparse basis directly onto the measurement basis. QCS executes the support-set search at the quantum level without consuming measurement trials. The logarithmic penalty vanishes, compressing the required measurement number from the classical bound to M =O(K) and reducing reconstruction from ill posed optimization to linear estimation. We experimentally validate QCS using frequency and time domain sparse signals, confirming that the measurement number scales linearly with sparsity and decouples entirely from the signal dimension. Our work provides a physical pathway toward ultimate information acquisition efficiency, with broad implications for sensing, imaging, and communication.
tldr: Quantum compressed sensing reduces the number of measurements required for signal recovery from O(K log(N/K)) to O(K) by encoding the signal into a quantum probe and using domain-alignment evolution.
motivation: To overcome the logarithmic overhead in classical compressed sensing and achieve ultimate information acquisition efficiency.
method: The signal is encoded into a quantum probe state, then a unitary domain-alignment evolution maps the sparse basis directly onto the measurement basis, enabling support-set search at the quantum level without consuming measurement trials.
result: Experimental validation with frequency and time domain sparse signals shows that the required measurement number scales linearly with sparsity K and is independent of signal dimension N.
conclusion: QCS provides a physical pathway to ultimate information acquisition efficiency, with implications for sensing, imaging, and communication.

title: Dynamical Aspects Of Steady-state Subradiance: Detailed Balance And Its Breakdown
authors: Athreya Shankar, Simon B. J\"ager, Jarrod T. Reilly, Raphael Kaubruegger, Murray J. Holland, Walter Hahn
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamics of dissipative many-body quantum systems sometimes admit an emergent classical description in terms of a Markov chain even though the corresponding state space contains highly entangled states. In particular, a bad-cavity laser is a paradigm system whose dynamics can be formulated as a Markov chain in a two-dimensional state space spanned by collective angular momentum states. In this article, we investigate the connection between a dissipative phase transition that occurs in the subradiant regime of this system in the large atom number limit, and the properties of the underlying Markov chain. In one of the phases, the Markov chain approaches the detailed-balance condition with increasing atom number [MATH] and hence becomes effectively time-reversible. This is caused by a collective atomic emission process that effectively reduces the Markov chain to one dimension. In the other phase, we find the emergence of time-asymmetric probability currents in the two-dimensional state space that signals a breakdown of detailed balance. This is accompanied by a macroscopic internal entropy production rate in the Markov chain that scales extensively with the atom number [MATH]. An observable consequence of the probability currents is a self-pulsing of the cavity light output in this phase, which can be detected as an anti-correlation dip in the intensity correlation function.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in a bad-cavity laser, revealing that in the subradiant regime the underlying Markov chain either satisfies detailed balance (time-reversible) or breaks it with macroscopic entropy production and self-pulsing.
motivation: To understand the connection between dissipative phase transitions and the properties of emergent classical Markov chain descriptions in many-body quantum systems, particularly in the subradiant regime of a bad-cavity laser.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics of a bad-cavity laser as a Markov chain in a two-dimensional state space of collective angular momentum states, and analyze the detailed-balance condition and probability currents as a function of atom number.
result: In one phase, the Markov chain approaches detailed balance and becomes effectively one-dimensional due to collective emission; in the other phase, detailed balance breaks down, leading to time-asymmetric probability currents and an entropy production rate scaling with atom number, observable as self-pulsing in cavity output.
conclusion: The work provides a classical Markov-chain perspective on a quantum dissipative phase transition, with implications for understanding irreversibility and entropy production in open quantum systems, and suggests experimental signatures via intensity correlation measurements.

title: Propagation Of Conditional Nonclassical Reservoir States During Quantum Decoherence
authors: Jargalsaikhan Artag, Koki Awaya, Takumi Kanezashi, Haruya Nagata, Daisuke Tsukayama, Moe Shimada, Jun-Ichi Shirakashi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoherence is usually described as the loss of local quantum coherence after tracing over environmental degrees of freedom. This reduced description, however, hides the reservoir state that carries the lost coherence. Here we show that spin-boson decoherence can write a postselectable nonclassical imprint into a structured bosonic reservoir. We map zero- and finite-temperature reservoirs to one-dimensional chains, evolve the joint qubit-reservoir state with tensor-network dynamics, and reconstruct the Wigner function of a time-adaptive leading collective reservoir coordinate after transverse qubit readout. The conditioned mapped-reservoir coordinate develops Wigner negativity and interference fringes that are strongly suppressed in the unconditional reservoir state. A parameter sweep shows that the spectral exponent and temperature control the visibility of this conditional nonclassicality, the mapped-chain excitation transport, and the degree to which a single collective coordinate captures the imprint. These results provide a branch-resolved phase-space picture of decoherence: the reservoir is not only a sink for qubit coherence, but can carry a measurement-conditioned nonclassical state in a collective mapped coordinate.
tldr: This paper shows that spin-boson decoherence can create a postselectable nonclassical state in a structured reservoir, revealing that the reservoir is not merely a sink but can carry measurement-conditioned quantum coherence.
motivation: To understand the reservoir's role in decoherence beyond being a sink for quantum coherence, and to explore whether nonclassical features can be conditionally imprinted and retrieved from the environment.
method: The authors map zero- and finite-temperature spin-boson reservoirs to one-dimensional chains, simulate joint qubit-reservoir dynamics using tensor-network methods, and reconstruct the Wigner function of a time-adaptive collective reservoir coordinate after transverse qubit readout.
result: The conditioned reservoir coordinate exhibits Wigner negativity and interference fringes that are absent in the unconditional state; the visibility of this nonclassicality depends on the spectral exponent and temperature, and a single collective coordinate can capture the imprint under certain conditions.
conclusion: The reservoir can carry a measurement-conditioned nonclassical state, providing a branch-resolved phase-space picture of decoherence and suggesting potential for reservoir engineering and quantum information processing.

title: Clifford-deformed Zero-rate Ldpc Codes With 50% Biased Noise Thresholds
authors: Jagannath Das, Sayandip Dhara, Pedro Medina, Arthur Pesah, Arpit Dua
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying single-qubit Clifford unitaries to a Pauli stabilizer code produces a Clifford-deformed variant whose stabilizers remain Pauli operators, but with locally rotated Pauli axes. Such deformations provide a simple way to tailor a fixed code to anisotropic noise, and have enabled unusually high thresholds under strongly biased dephasing. In this work, we discuss zero-rate quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, for which there exist Clifford-deformed variants where the number of biased logical operators scales slower than the distance, or there exists a basis of logical operators whose overlap satisfies certain scaling conditions; in this case, the code-capacity threshold for the Clifford-deformed variant under i.i.d. pure dephasing noise approaches 50%. This property provably explains previously known code examples with 50% biased noise thresholds, such as XY surface code, XZZX surface code, color code, as well as some 3D Clifford-deformed codes. As a concrete new example, we study Clifford deformations of the tile codes of Ref. [1]. Similar to the phase diagram of 50% thresholds for random Clifford deformations of the surface code in Ref. [2], we find a similar phase diagram for the tile codes. We also construct several translationally invariant deformations of the tile code with 50% thresholds, and present numerical evidence for improved performance at finite bias and under circuit-level noise. In the circuit-level setting, performance is governed by the residual bias after a full syndrome-extraction cycle, linking our simulations to phenomenological models commonly used to study Clifford-deformed codes. We estimate this residual bias for different qubit platforms by modeling microscopic implementations of tile-code syndrome extraction.
tldr: This paper shows that Clifford-deformed zero-rate LDPC codes can achieve 50% biased noise thresholds under pure dephasing noise, with applications to quantum error correction.
motivation: To understand how Clifford deformations can improve the performance of quantum LDPC codes under biased noise, and to identify conditions for achieving 50% thresholds.
method: The authors analyze the logical operator structure of Clifford-deformed codes, derive scaling conditions for biased logical operators, and perform numerical simulations of tile codes under circuit-level noise.
result: They prove that if the number of biased logical operators scales slower than the distance, or if logical operators satisfy certain overlap conditions, the code-capacity threshold approaches 50%. They demonstrate this for tile codes and find a phase diagram similar to surface codes.
conclusion: Clifford-deformed LDPC codes are promising for biased noise, and the residual bias after syndrome extraction governs circuit-level performance, linking to phenomenological models.

title: Single Spatio-Temporal Mode Bright Twin-Beam Source Across The Near- And Mid-Infrared
authors: Gabriel Demontigny, Patrick Cusson, Amauri Perraton Elorza, Esteban Murillo Zapata, Eli Martel, Andrei Rasputnyi, Maria Chekhova, St\'ephane Virally, Denis Seletskiy

Group-delay dispersion of the pump drives a continuous transition from single-mode operation to a controlled multimode regime, consistent with the temporal gain window departing from the inverse phase-matching bandwidth. Strong non-degeneracy of the source (signal at 1.37 um, idler at 4.0 um, [MATH] fs duration) decouples a mid-infrared interaction wavelength, which overlaps with molecular vibrational resonances, from a near-infrared detection band, establishing a practical platform for quantum-enhanced metrology, nonlinear interferometry, and mid-infrared spectroscopic sensing. motivation: To develop a practical entangled photon source that operates across near- and mid-infrared wavelengths for applications in quantum metrology and spectroscopy.
method: Type-0 parametric down-conversion in periodically-poled lithium niobate at MHz repetition rate, with pump pulse duration tuning the Schmidt number; characterization via photon-number statistics and singular-value decomposition.
result: Single-mode to controlled multimode operation achieved; up to 95-97% of entanglement resource allocated to occupational degrees of freedom; signal at 1.37 μm, idler at 4.0 μm.
conclusion: The source provides a platform for quantum-enhanced metrology and mid-infrared spectroscopic sensing, with clear separation of modal and occupational entanglement.

title: Thermodynamic Invariants Of Coupled Channels: A Many-Channel Tolman-Ehrenfest Effect
authors: Benjamin Hamblin, Victor Calo, Klaus Regenauer-Lieb
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When multiple thermodynamic channels are coupled, single-channel equilibrium conditions fail. Extending the Tolman--Ehrenfest effect to the entropy manifold, we derive the unique [MATH]-channel invariant [MATH], where [MATH] is the holonomy of the Ruppeiner connection. For the granular volume--stress ensemble, Rowe's dilatancy ratio and energy restriction emerge as geometric consequences of the off-diagonal curvature [MATH], and the 60-year puzzle of state-dependent [MATH] is resolved: the correction [MATH] reaches [MATH] near jamming. The prediction [MATH] across a shear band is experimentally testable.
tldr: This paper derives thermodynamic invariants for coupled channels, extending the Tolman-Ehrenfest effect to the entropy manifold and resolving a long-standing puzzle in granular mechanics.
motivation: To understand equilibrium conditions when multiple thermodynamic channels are coupled, as single-channel conditions fail, and to resolve the 60-year puzzle of state-dependent dilatancy in granular materials.
method: The authors extend the Tolman-Ehrenfest effect to the entropy manifold, deriving a many-channel invariant using the holonomy of the Ruppeiner connection, and apply it to the granular volume-stress ensemble.
result: They find that Rowe's dilatancy ratio and energy restriction emerge as geometric consequences of off-diagonal curvature, and the correction to the dilatancy angle reaches 30° near jamming, with a testable prediction across a shear band.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric framework for coupled thermodynamic channels, with implications for granular mechanics and potentially for information thermodynamics where coupled channels appear.

title: Breaking The Finite-Sample Barrier In Entropy Coupling
authors: Jun Chen Shahab Asoodeh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.16229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dependence among marginally constrained observations can break a finite-sample barrier. To formalize this phenomenon, we introduce the [MATH], the minimum conditional entropy [MATH] over all joint distributions with prescribed discrete marginals [MATH] and [MATH]. Unlike classical formulations based on independent observations, our model allows [MATH] to be arbitrarily dependent while keeping each marginal fixed. This enlarged coupling space reveals a sharp dichotomy: independent observations reduce residual uncertainty exponentially, whereas dependent observations can eliminate it exactly after finitely many samples. We characterize this zero-entropy regime through necessary and sufficient conditions and give concrete structural criteria under which it occurs. In particular, under mild support assumptions, zero entropy is achieved with [MATH] observations, where [MATH] is the minimum nonzero mass of [MATH]. We also develop a greedy algorithm with monotone approximation guarantees for computing [MATH]. Finally, we show that the same framework formalizes finite-sample limits in distribution-matching representation learning and randomness extraction, where zero entropy corresponds to exact recovery and exact extraction.
tldr: This paper introduces a new entropy coupling framework that shows dependent observations can achieve zero conditional entropy after finitely many samples, breaking the exponential decay barrier of independent observations.
motivation: To formalize how dependence among marginally constrained observations can eliminate residual uncertainty exactly after a finite number of samples, contrasting with the exponential decay in independent settings.
method: The authors define a minimum conditional entropy over joint distributions with fixed discrete marginals, allowing arbitrary dependence. They characterize the zero-entropy regime via necessary and sufficient conditions and develop a greedy algorithm with monotone approximation guarantees.
result: Zero conditional entropy is achieved with at most 1/p_min observations, where p_min is the minimum nonzero marginal probability. The framework also applies to distribution-matching representation learning and randomness extraction.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for finite-sample exact recovery in tasks like representation learning and randomness extraction, with implications for information-theoretic limits in dependent data settings.

title: Beyond Unitary Quantum Simulation: Open-System Approaches To Quantum Chemistry Toward Quantum Advantage
authors: Michael Marthaler, Elias Zapusek, Florentin Reiter
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum simulation is widely regarded as one of the most promising routes to genuine quantum advantage, yet most existing approaches to quantum chemistry are formulated in terms of closed-system, unitary dynamics and ground-state preparation within the Born--Oppenheimer approximation. In this review, we discuss a broader perspective motivated by the observation that naturally occurring quantum systems are rarely isolated and often reach physically relevant states only through relaxation, decoherence, and thermalization. We first examine what is and is not known about exponential quantum advantage in chemistry, emphasizing that coherent Hamiltonian simulation provides the clearest formal case for speed-up, while many open questions remain for realistic problems. We then discuss how dissipation might ideally be integrated into quantum chemistry on a fault-tolerant quantum computer, using recent proposals for chemically motivated dynamical simulation as a guiding vision. More generally, we highlight the practical appeal of this approach to enhancing the robustness of quantum algorithms.
tldr: This review discusses open-system approaches to quantum chemistry simulation, emphasizing dissipation and decoherence as resources rather than obstacles.
motivation: Most quantum chemistry simulations assume closed-system unitary dynamics, but natural quantum systems are open and reach relevant states through relaxation and thermalization.
method: The paper reviews existing literature on quantum advantage in chemistry, contrasts coherent Hamiltonian simulation with open-system approaches, and outlines proposals for integrating dissipation into fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
result: Coherent Hamiltonian simulation provides the clearest formal case for exponential speedup, but many open questions remain for realistic problems; dissipation can enhance robustness and potentially enable new types of quantum advantage.
conclusion: Open-system approaches may be a practical route to quantum advantage in chemistry, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed to realize their potential.

title: Short-time Critical Dynamics In The Classical Cubic Dimer Model
authors: Hu-Xiao Peng, Zheng Yan, Shuai Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical dimer model on the cubic lattice hosts a columnar ordered phase and a disordered Coulomb phase, separated by a continuous phase transition that lies beyond the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. While its equilibrium critical properties have been extensively studied, the nonequilibrium critical dynamics of this model--particularly in the short-time regime--remains largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate the short-time critical dynamics near the transition using large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. By quenching the system from both ordered and disordered initial states with vanishing initial correlation length, we analyze the scaling behaviors of the order parameter and its time correlation function in the short-time stage. From these scaling behaviors, we accurately determine the critical temperature [MATH] and the static critical exponent [MATH] according to the scaling theory of the short-time dynamics. These results are in excellent agreement with previous equilibrium studies. Moreover, we extract the dynamic critical exponent [MATH] and, notably, find a negative critical initial slip exponent [MATH]. This unusual negative value contrasts sharply with the positive [MATH] typically observed in conventional critical dynamics. We attribute this anomalous behavior to the combined effects of the emergent SO(5) symmetry at criticality and the local U(1) gauge constraint (Gauss law), which enforces a conserved diffusive dynamics and enhances fluctuations in the short-time regime. Our results provide the first comprehensive characterization of nonequilibrium short-time criticality in the three-dimensional dimer model, shedding new light on the universal dynamical features of phase transitions beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson framework.
tldr: This paper studies short-time critical dynamics in the classical cubic dimer model, finding a negative critical initial slip exponent due to emergent SO(5) symmetry and gauge constraints.
motivation: To explore nonequilibrium critical dynamics in a model with a continuous phase transition beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm, which has been studied in equilibrium but not in short-time dynamics.
method: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations quenching the system from ordered and disordered initial states with vanishing initial correlation length, analyzing scaling behaviors of order parameter and time correlation function.
result: Accurately determined critical temperature and static critical exponent, extracted dynamic critical exponent, and discovered a negative critical initial slip exponent, contrasting with conventional positive values.
conclusion: Provides first comprehensive characterization of nonequilibrium short-time criticality in 3D dimer model, revealing universal dynamical features beyond standard framework.

title: Synthesis And Optimization Of Encoding Circuits For Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Tom Peham, Matthew Steinberg, Robert Wille, Sascha Heu{\ss}en
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preparing arbitrary logical states is a central primitive for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation and the cost of encoded-state preparation contributes directly to the overall resource overhead. This makes the synthesis of efficient general-state encoding circuits an important problem, particularly with respect to two-qubit gate count and circuit depth. Yet the synthesis of such encoders has been studied less extensively than general Clifford circuit synthesis or the preparation of specific logical Pauli-eigenstates. In this work, we develop methods for synthesizing efficient encoders for arbitrary stabilizer codes. We formulate encoder synthesis as a search over stabilizer tableaus and introduce greedy and rollout-based algorithms that exploit the freedom among stabilizer-equivalent realizations of the same encoding isometry. For code families with a modular structure, such as generalized concatenated and holographic codes, we show how large encoders can be assembled from optimized local constituent encoders, and we use SMT-based exact synthesis to obtain optimal local circuits for small instances. We further evaluate the proposed methods on a broad set of stabilizer codes, including holographic and quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, and compare them against recent encoder-synthesis methods and existing constructions from the literature, obtaining improvements of up to 43% in two-qubit gate count and up to 70% in depth. Our results support the optimization of encoded-state preparation in several fault-tolerant quantum-computing schemes, and all methods are openly available as part of the Munich Quantum Toolkit.
tldr: This paper presents methods for synthesizing efficient encoding circuits for arbitrary stabilizer codes, focusing on reducing two-qubit gate count and depth for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Preparing arbitrary logical states is a key primitive for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, and the cost of encoded-state preparation contributes directly to overall resource overhead. Efficient synthesis of encoding circuits is less studied than general Clifford circuit synthesis.
method: The authors formulate encoder synthesis as a search over stabilizer tableaus and introduce greedy and rollout-based algorithms exploiting stabilizer-equivalent realizations. For modular code families, they assemble large encoders from optimized local constituent encoders using SMT-based exact synthesis for small instances.
result: The proposed methods achieve improvements of up to 43% in two-qubit gate count and up to 70% in depth compared to existing methods, evaluated on a broad set of stabilizer codes including holographic and qLDPC codes.
conclusion: The results support optimization of encoded-state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum computing schemes, and all methods are openly available as part of the Munich Quantum Toolkit.

title: Towards Deploying Optimistic Quantum Fourier Transforms: An Architecture-Algorithm Co-Design Study
authors: Pedro L. S. Lopes
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an architecture-algorithm co-design study of the Optimistic Quantum Fourier Transform (OQFT) under a surface-code fault-tolerant execution model for reconfigurable neutral-atom hardware. Analyzing the OQFT structure, particularly its reliance on phase-gradient resources and small-scale blocks, highlights architectural requirements for resource mobility and parallel execution. Guided by that, we introduce a hot-zone architecture that decouples data storage from processing and dynamically routes mobile resource packages (magic-state factories, bridge qubits, and phase-gradient registers) to stationary data regions. To expose dominant costs, we route rotation insertions via catalytic phase-gradient addition and heuristically micro-schedule ripple-carry adders to patch-level moves. Under this model, leading Gidney~ and Cuccaro~ adders have similar space-time volume but require different levels of parallelism. At the algorithm level, the five-layer OQFT shows a tunable parallelism/latency trade-off: two hot zones match serial-QFT latency, four hot zones roughly halve runtime, and additional hot zones asymptotically approach constant-time execution at substantial resource cost. Across 256-2048-bit instances, the requirements for half-time performance converge to about 500 additional logical ancillae and a peak parallelism of 128 logical qubits. We also identify broader algorithm-architecture bottlenecks, including endianness mismatches between phase-gradient and data registers, addressed via cyclic phase-gradient swaps and alternating QFT reflections. Scoped to surface codes and cultivation-only magic-state factories, our analysis identifies reaction-limited operation and parallelism demand as primary drivers of resource estimation and establishes a generalizable foundation for primitive-based architectural studies.
tldr: This paper presents an architecture-algorithm co-design study of the Optimistic Quantum Fourier Transform under a surface-code fault-tolerant execution model for reconfigurable neutral-atom hardware.
motivation: To optimize the implementation of quantum Fourier transforms on fault-tolerant quantum hardware by co-designing the algorithm and architecture.
method: The authors analyze the OQFT structure, introduce a hot-zone architecture with mobile resource packages, and use catalytic phase-gradient addition and heuristic micro-scheduling of ripple-carry adders.
result: The five-layer OQFT shows a tunable parallelism/latency trade-off; two hot zones match serial-QFT latency, four hot zones halve runtime, and more asymptotically approach constant time at substantial resource cost.
conclusion: The analysis identifies reaction-limited operation and parallelism demand as primary drivers of resource estimation, establishing a foundation for primitive-based architectural studies.

title: Fire And Ice: Partially Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing With Selective State Filtering
authors: Ben W. Reichardt, David Aasen, Rui Chao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an error-corrected quantum computation scheme based on concatenating the five-qubit Laflamme code onto the four-qubit Iceberg code. The approach skates a thin line: it is explicitly not fault tolerant, risking higher logical error rates, and it relies on selective filtering to prepare encoded states for error correction, risking significant overhead. Yet, at realistic simulated noise rates, the scheme is reliable and resource efficient. It forges a practical path toward scalable quantum computation.
tldr: The paper proposes a non-fault-tolerant quantum error correction scheme concatenating the five-qubit Laflamme code onto the four-qubit Iceberg code, using selective state filtering to achieve practical reliability at realistic noise rates.
motivation: To develop a resource-efficient quantum error correction scheme that is practical for near-term devices, even if it sacrifices full fault tolerance.
method: Concatenation of the five-qubit Laflamme code onto the four-qubit Iceberg code, combined with selective state filtering for encoded state preparation.
result: The scheme is not fault-tolerant but shows reliable performance and resource efficiency under realistic simulated noise rates.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical path toward scalable quantum computation by balancing error correction overhead and fault tolerance requirements.

title: Measurement-Efficient Variational Quantum Linear Solver For Carleman-Linearized Nonlinear Dynamics
authors: Pai Wang Yunya Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present hybrid quantum-classical pipelines for solving the Duffing equation that leverage Carleman linearization and the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS). First, we demonstrate that Carleman linearization accurately approximates the weakly nonlinear Duffing equation, with errors diminishing as the truncation order increases. Next, across IBM and Xanadu platforms, we deploy VQLS with symmetry-grouped Hadamard Test evaluations under both global and local cost formulations, compare distinct Hermitianization within a common cost framework, and benchmark hardware-efficient ansatz architectures under a fixed Hermitianization. Across block-banded test cases, each method achieves near-unity fidelity and vanishing relative residuals. These results show that topology-agnostic ansatz, optimized Hermitianization, and efficient cost formulation enable VQLS to recover quantum states proportional to classical solutions for Carleman-structured systems, providing a portable recipe for quantum-in-the-loop simulation of nonlinear dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline using Carleman linearization and VQLS to solve the Duffing equation, focusing on measurement efficiency and ansatz design.
motivation: To enable quantum-in-the-loop simulation of nonlinear dynamics by combining Carleman linearization with variational quantum linear solvers.
method: Carleman linearization is applied to the Duffing equation, then solved via VQLS with symmetry-grouped Hadamard tests, comparing global/local cost functions and Hermitianization strategies.
result: Near-unity fidelity and vanishing residuals are achieved across block-banded test cases, demonstrating that topology-agnostic ansatz and optimized Hermitianization enable accurate recovery of classical solutions.
conclusion: The approach provides a portable recipe for quantum simulation of nonlinear dynamics, but its relevance to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is limited.

title: Quantum Feature Pyramid Gating For Seismic Image Segmentation
authors: Jyotsna Sharma Taha Gharaibeh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate salt-body delineation is essential for seismic interpretation because salt structures distort wave propagation, complicate velocity-model building, obscure reservoir geometry, and increase uncertainty in exploration and drilling decisions. Although hybrid quantum-classical models have shown competitive performance on small-scale image-classification tasks, their value for dense, pixel-level geophysical prediction remains largely untested. This work introduces quantum feature gating, a hybrid segmentation architecture that embeds a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) at feature-fusion points within an encoder-decoder pipeline. A 4-qubit, 2-layer PQC with data re-uploading computes a learned convex combination of lateral and top-down features at each Feature Pyramid Network merge point. A global-average-pooling layer maps encoder features to a fixed 4-dimensional quantum input, decoupling the 72-parameter quantum budget from backbone size and image resolution. The method is evaluated on the 2018 TGS Salt Identification Challenge using 4,000 seismic images at 101 x 101 resolution, across two integration topologies, eight circuit variants, and six encoders with 8M to 118M parameters under five-fold cross-validation. In a controlled EfficientNetV2-L ablation at 256 x 256 resolution, replacing the three Quantum FPN Gates with element-wise addition while holding the encoder, loss schedule, splits, and threshold search fixed reduces mean IoU from 0.9389 to 0.8404, a 9.85 percentage-point gap. Inserting the same circuit as skip-connection attention in a custom U-Net improves IoU by 0.88 points over the SolidUNet baseline, showing that the PQC contribution depends on where and what it gates. These results provide controlled evidence that quantum feature fusion can improve dense seismic segmentation.
tldr: This paper introduces a hybrid quantum-classical segmentation architecture using parameterized quantum circuits for feature gating in seismic image segmentation, showing improved IoU over classical baselines.
motivation: To test whether hybrid quantum-classical models can improve dense pixel-level geophysical prediction, specifically salt-body delineation in seismic images.
method: A 4-qubit, 2-layer PQC with data re-uploading is embedded at feature-fusion points in a Feature Pyramid Network within an encoder-decoder pipeline, with global average pooling to map encoder features to quantum input.
result: Replacing quantum gates with element-wise addition in EfficientNetV2-L reduced mean IoU from 0.9389 to 0.8404; inserting the circuit as skip-connection attention in a U-Net improved IoU by 0.88 points over baseline.
conclusion: Quantum feature fusion can improve dense seismic segmentation, but the benefit depends on where and what the PQC gates; further work is needed to generalize to other domains and larger quantum circuits.

title: Orthogonal Polynomials And The MacWilliams Transform For Permutation-Invariant Qudit Codes
authors: Ian Teixeira
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an explicit formula for the intrinsic MacWilliams transform for permutation-invariant qudit codes. Such codes naturally live in symmetric power representations, where the relevant error sectors are determined by the irreducible decomposition of the conjugation action on the associated operator space. Using the multiplicity-free structure of this decomposition and the corresponding intertwiner algebra, we identify the intrinsic MacWilliams matrix with a finite Racah transform. The entries are given by a terminating hypergeometric series, and the rows of the matrix are Racah orthogonal polynomials with parameters determined explicitly by the block length and local dimension. Computing the spectrum of the degree-one twirl reveals that this spectrum lies on an affine quadratic lattice. Then we derive a tridiagonal multiplication rule from the representation theory of the adjoint sector. As consequences, we obtain closed-form orthogonality, detailed-balance, and involutivity identities for the transform. The resulting formula supplies an explicit MacWilliams matrix for computing linear programming bounds on permutation-invariant qudit codes.
tldr: The paper derives an explicit MacWilliams transform for permutation-invariant qudit codes using Racah orthogonal polynomials.
motivation: To provide a closed-form MacWilliams matrix for computing linear programming bounds on permutation-invariant qudit codes, which are important for quantum error correction.
method: The authors use representation theory of symmetric powers and intertwiner algebras to identify the MacWilliams matrix with a finite Racah transform, deriving entries via terminating hypergeometric series.
result: They obtain explicit orthogonality, detailed-balance, and involutivity identities for the transform, and show the spectrum of the degree-one twirl lies on an affine quadratic lattice.
conclusion: The work supplies a practical tool for bounding code parameters, but its direct connection to the user's research interests in thermodynamics, foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is limited.

title: Diagonal Adaptive Non-local Observables On Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Huan-Hsin Tseng, Yan Li, Hsin-Yi Lin, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANOs) have shown that making quantum observables dynamic can substantially enlarge the function space of Variational Quantum Algorithms, partly shifting hardware demands from circuit synthesis to measurement design. However, this advantage is accompanied by a steep increase in the number of parameters, as well as the classical optimization cost for varying general Hermitian observables. We propose a special form of ANO that significantly reduces this burden by considering only diagonal observables paired with quantum circuits. Mathematically, this is equivalent to the full ANO of a large parameter space since diagonal matrices are canonical representatives of the ANO space modulo unitary similarity. As a result, Diagonal ANO retains the same capability of full ANO while reducing [MATH]-local observable complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] and lowering the corresponding measurement-side classical computation. In this sense, diagonal ANO preserves much of the benefit of full ANO while encompassing conventional VQCs as a special case.
tldr: The paper proposes Diagonal Adaptive Non-local Observables to reduce parameter and measurement complexity in variational quantum algorithms while preserving expressivity.
motivation: Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANOs) enhance the function space of variational quantum algorithms but introduce a steep increase in parameters and classical optimization cost. The authors aim to reduce this burden.
method: They restrict ANOs to diagonal observables paired with quantum circuits, showing that diagonal matrices are canonical representatives of the ANO space modulo unitary similarity, thus retaining full ANO capability.
result: Diagonal ANO reduces the local observable complexity from exponential to polynomial and lowers measurement-side classical computation, while encompassing conventional VQCs as a special case.
conclusion: Diagonal ANO preserves the benefits of full ANO with significantly reduced resource requirements, offering a practical improvement for variational quantum algorithms.

title: Coherent States Of Non-Null Torus Knots
authors: Ion Vasile Vancea Gabriel Canadas Da Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct coherent states for the quantized electromagnetic field that correspond to the classical non-null torus knot solutions of Maxwell's equations in vacuum. We derive the displacement operators from the general relation between classical fields and coherent state amplitudes and verify the defining properties of coherent states through direct computation. We determine the observables of the model: field expectation values, energy density, Poynting vector, helicity, photon number, quadrature uncertainties, and correlation functions, and calculate their expectation values in the knotted coherent states in terms of the integer parameters [MATH] of the classical solutions. As an example, we particularize the construction in the case of the Hopfion coherent state. These results establish the quantum-classical correspondence for this type of vacuum topological electromagnetic systems.
tldr: This paper constructs coherent states of the quantized electromagnetic field corresponding to classical non-null torus knot solutions of Maxwell's equations.
motivation: To establish a quantum-classical correspondence for topological electromagnetic systems, specifically knotted light fields.
method: Derives displacement operators from the relation between classical fields and coherent state amplitudes, then verifies coherent state properties and computes observables.
result: Explicit expressions for field expectation values, energy density, Poynting vector, helicity, photon number, quadrature uncertainties, and correlation functions in terms of knot parameters.
conclusion: Provides a foundation for studying quantum properties of knotted light, with potential applications in topological photonics and quantum information.

title: Strong Universality Class In Disordered Systems
authors: Henrique A Lima, Kaue Hermann, Ismael S. S. Carrasco, Jairo R. L. de Almeida, Fernando A. Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disordered systems are very rich laboratories for exploring complex systems. In particular, disordered magnetic systems have been extremely important in the last five decades for understanding a wide range of phenomena. In this work, we use the Edwards-Anderson Hamiltonian to obtain the thermodynamic properties of disordered magnetic systems. In this way, we conduct a systematic investigation of magnetization, correlation functions, order parameter, and fractal dimensions, in function of disorder. In this context, the autocorrelation function for order--parameter fluctuations, introduced by Fisher ( Journal of Mathematical Physics 5, 944322 (1964)), provides an important mathematical framework for understanding the second-order phase transition at equilibrium. However, his analysis is restricted to a Euclidean space of dimension [MATH], and an exponent [MATH] is introduced to correct the spatial behavior of the correlation function at [MATH]. In recent work, Lima et al ( Phys. Rev. E 110, L062107 (2024)) demonstrated that at [MATH] a fractal analysis is necessary for a complete description of the correlation function. We use Monte Carlo simulations to validate analytical results and to show how disorder alters critical exponents , giving rise to different universality classes. On the other hand, there is a subgroup of critical exponents and fractal dimensions that are invariant with disorder. This subgroup heralds a strong universality class.
tldr: This paper studies universality classes in disordered magnetic systems using the Edwards-Anderson Hamiltonian and Monte Carlo simulations, identifying a subgroup of critical exponents invariant with disorder.
motivation: To understand how disorder affects critical exponents and fractal dimensions in magnetic systems, and to identify universal behavior that is independent of disorder strength.
method: Analytical calculations based on the Edwards-Anderson Hamiltonian and Monte Carlo simulations to compute magnetization, correlation functions, order parameter, and fractal dimensions.
result: Disorder alters critical exponents, giving rise to different universality classes, but a subgroup of exponents and fractal dimensions remains invariant, defining a strong universality class.
conclusion: The findings provide a deeper understanding of phase transitions in disordered systems and suggest that certain universal properties are robust to disorder.

title: Quantum Circuit Synthesis Using An Exact T Library
authors: Hanyu Wang, Mingfei Yu, Xinrui Wu, Jason Cong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum circuit synthesis, T gates supplied via magic states dominate space-time cost, while Clifford gates incur negligible overhead. Conventional flows minimize AND count in an {XOR, AND, NOT} basis as a proxy for T, which neglects phase cancellation and can be far from T-optimal. We instead formulate an exact T synthesis problem and canonicalize Boolean functions under Clifford equivalence. By precomputing T-optimal implementations up to seven variables and developing a customized mapper, we reduce the T count by up to 14.3% on EPFL benchmarks and improve the T counts of several cryptographic modules by up to 40%.
tldr: This paper presents a method for exact T-count optimization in fault-tolerant quantum circuit synthesis by precomputing T-optimal implementations for small Boolean functions and using a custom mapper.
motivation: Existing T-count optimization methods minimize AND count as a proxy, which neglects phase cancellation and yields suboptimal T counts. The authors aim to directly minimize T gates for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: They formulate an exact T synthesis problem, canonicalize Boolean functions under Clifford equivalence, precompute T-optimal implementations for up to seven variables, and develop a customized mapper to apply these implementations.
result: The method reduces T count by up to 14.3% on EPFL benchmarks and up to 40% on several cryptographic modules compared to conventional flows.
conclusion: Exact T synthesis can significantly improve T-count efficiency, but the approach is limited to small functions; future work may extend to larger functions or integrate with higher-level synthesis.

title: About Time: Observation Of Time-Reflection At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal (electrical & Computer Eng. Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Noa Konforty (solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Physics Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Oded Schiller (electrical & Computer Eng. Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Maxwell J. Tolchin (department Of Materials Science Engineering, Pennsylvania State University, USA), Tony Yasniger (solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Physics Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Michael Birk (solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, The Norman Seiden Multidisciplinary Program In Nano-Science And Nano-Technology, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Alexander Palatnik (solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Physics Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Soham Saha (argonne National Laboratory, Lemont, IL, USA), Pavel Sidorenko (electrical & Computer Eng. Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Jon-Paul Maria (department Of Materials Science Engineering, Pennsylvania State University, USA), Yonatan Plotnik (solid State Institute, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel, Physics Department, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Mordechai Segev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-reflection occurs when a wave is propagating in a medium undergoing a large and abrupt change in its properties: the original wave splits into a time-refracted wave and a time-reflected wave, each displaying different features. The time-refracted wave continues along its original course but experiences a frequency shift, whereas the time-reflected wave is propagating backwards in space with a reversed phase, also with a shifted frequency. These phenomena are fundamental to any wave system, but the most interesting are electromagnetic (EM) waves, specifically at optical frequencies, where they can couple to light-matter interactions. However, time-reflection of EM waves was thus far observed only at RF frequencies, never at optical frequencies. This is because time-reflection requires an order-unity variation of the refractive index occurring faster than a single wave cycle, and conventional optical nonlinearities are either too weak or too slow by orders of magnitude. Here, we present the first observation of time-reflection at optical frequencies. We induce an order-unity refractive-index change with sub-cycle duration, observe the time-reflection, and study its fundamental properties. These results provide an experimental pathway to experimenting with time-interfaces, generating photonic time-crystals and exploring new regimes of light-matter interaction in time-varying media.
tldr: First experimental observation of time-reflection of electromagnetic waves at optical frequencies using an ultrafast refractive index change.
motivation: Time-reflection had been observed only at RF frequencies; demonstrating it at optical frequencies opens new regimes for light-matter interaction and photonic time-crystals.
method: Induced an order-unity refractive index change with sub-cycle duration in a tailored medium, then probed the wave splitting into time-refracted and time-reflected components.
result: Observed time-reflected waves propagating backwards with reversed phase and frequency shift, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Enables experimental study of time-interfaces, photonic time-crystals, and novel light-matter interactions in time-varying media.

title: Chiral-Mode Control Around A Hermitian Diabolic Point In Discrete Non-Hermitian Coupled Resonators
authors: Kota Yagi, Takahiro Uemura, Yuto Moritake, Adam Mock, Masaya Notomi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the prospect of chiral-mode control in compact photonic systems, we analyze discrete coupled single-mode resonators. Using the minimal three-resonator model, we show that an infinitesimal complex onsite perturbation near a Hermitian diabolic point (DP) induces chiral-mode selection, governed by what we term an asymptotic exceptional point (AEP). Here, an AEP denotes a Hermitian DP equipped with a non-Hermitian perturbation that induces an asymptotically defective effective Hamiltonian. The eigenvectors coalesce in the asymptotic limit toward the DP, although the Hamiltonian at the point itself remains diagonalizable. Operationally, this AEP response realizes chirality switching from an achiral state to a chiral state. The associated eigenvalue response exhibits the anomalous fractional-power scaling [MATH], distinct from the square-root response of an ordinary exceptional point (EP). We further show that, in a broader two-parameter perturbation space, ordinary EPs lie on exceptional-line branches that meet at the AEP. A finitebias control sweep crosses these branches at an EP pair, enabling chirality reversal between opposite chiral states. The central message is therefore that the AEP organizes two related routes for chirality switching: direct switching from an achiral state to a chiral state via the AEP, and switching between opposite chiral states via an EP pair in the vicinity of the AEP. Within a finite-resolution averaging model, these two operating points exhibit different practical performance characteristics, and under sufficiently high control resolution, the AEP operating point can become more favorable than the EP-pair operating point, suggesting a route toward compact and low-energy chiral photonic devices.
tldr: This paper studies chiral-mode control in non-Hermitian coupled resonators using asymptotic exceptional points, but does not directly address the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve chiral-mode control in compact photonic systems for potential applications in photonic devices.
method: The authors analyze a minimal three-resonator model with complex onsite perturbations near a Hermitian diabolic point, introducing the concept of an asymptotic exceptional point (AEP).
result: An infinitesimal non-Hermitian perturbation near a diabolic point induces chiral-mode selection with anomalous fractional-power eigenvalue scaling, and ordinary exceptional points lie on branches meeting at the AEP.
conclusion: The AEP enables two routes for chirality switching, with potential advantages for low-energy chiral photonic devices under high control resolution.

title: Ultralong Pump-probe Movies Of Magnon And Phonon Dynamics From Ultrafast Generation To Microsecond Relaxation
authors: Riku Shibata, Shun Fujii, Shinichi Watanabe
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The long lifetimes of magnons and phonons make them attractive for information-processing devices, highlighting the importance of visualizing their spatiotemporal dynamics from generation through relaxation. Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is a powerful tool for investigating their early-stage dynamics after impulsive excitation; however, their long-lived nature makes it challenging to comprehensively track their evolution across all relevant time scales while maintaining sufficient temporal resolution. Here, we demonstrate spatiotemporal tracking of magnon and phonon dynamics over more than seven orders of magnitude in time, from 500 femtoseconds to 20 microseconds, using [MATH] sampled time points enabled by the highly precise time base of optical frequency combs. The resulting spatiotemporal movie, consisting of [MATH] frames, captures their generation, coherent motion, propagation, and relaxation, providing a powerful platform for exploring their full dynamical evolution.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ultralong pump-probe movies of magnon and phonon dynamics from femtoseconds to microseconds using optical frequency combs.
motivation: To visualize the full spatiotemporal evolution of magnons and phonons across all relevant time scales, which is challenging due to their long lifetimes.
method: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy with a highly precise time base from optical frequency combs, enabling sampling over seven orders of magnitude in time.
result: Spatiotemporal tracking of magnon and phonon dynamics from 500 fs to 20 μs, capturing generation, coherent motion, propagation, and relaxation.
conclusion: The technique provides a powerful platform for exploring the full dynamical evolution of long-lived quasiparticles, with potential applications in information-processing devices.

title: Nonlocal Optical Response And Surface Susceptibilities: A Systematic Derivation Via Spatial Moment Expansion
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Zolla
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a systematic theory connecting the nonlocal response kernel of a homogeneous medium to its effective surface susceptibilities for an arbitrary curved interface. Starting from the most general tensorial nonlocal constitutive relation and combining a spatial moment expansion with a distributional thin-layer limit, we show that the full complexity of the interfacial response condenses, at leading order, into a single scalar: the surface susceptibility [MATH], equal for the tangential and normal components of the electric field. These quantities provide a constructive generalization of the Feibelman [MATH]-parameters to interfaces of arbitrary curvature, and the curvature corrections, proportional to the geometric invariants [MATH] (mean curvature) and [MATH] (Gaussian curvature), are derived explicitly. The formalism is illustrated on a comprehensive set of analytically tractable cases (planar, spherical, cylindrical, and ellipsoidal interfaces) for several kernel choices (Gaussian, Yukawa, tensorial Lorentz). Generalized Maxwell boundary conditions are established and compared with the classical Fresnel results.
tldr: This paper derives a systematic theory connecting nonlocal optical response of homogeneous media to effective surface susceptibilities for arbitrary curved interfaces.
motivation: To generalize the Feibelman d-parameters to interfaces of arbitrary curvature and provide a constructive formalism for nonlocal optical response.
method: Spatial moment expansion combined with a distributional thin-layer limit applied to the most general tensorial nonlocal constitutive relation.
result: The full complexity of interfacial response condenses into a single scalar surface susceptibility, with curvature corrections proportional to mean and Gaussian curvatures.
conclusion: The formalism yields generalized Maxwell boundary conditions and is illustrated on several geometries and kernel choices, extending classical Fresnel results.

title: Quantum Game Theory For 2 2 Games: A Mathematical Framework
authors: Veronica Umanit\`a Gloria Ferraris
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for quantum game theory applied to static 2x2 games, extending classical concepts to the quantum setting where players may employ arbitrary unitary operations (pure strategies) or probability measures over the continuous group SU(2) (mixed strategies). The Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein protocol is introduced as the standard implementation of quantum 2x2 games. We prove the existence of Nash equilibria for continuous quantum mixed strategies via a fixed-point argument, generalising the classical Nash theorem to the quantum case.
tldr: This paper develops a mathematical framework for quantum game theory applied to static 2x2 games, extending classical Nash equilibrium concepts to quantum strategies.
motivation: To provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for quantum game theory, which has been explored heuristically, and to prove existence of Nash equilibria for continuous quantum mixed strategies.
method: The authors use the Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein protocol to implement quantum 2x2 games and apply fixed-point arguments to prove existence of Nash equilibria for probability measures over SU(2).
result: They prove that Nash equilibria exist for continuous quantum mixed strategies, generalizing the classical Nash theorem to the quantum setting.
conclusion: The work establishes a solid mathematical basis for quantum game theory, but its direct relevance to the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is limited.

title: Bias Analysis And Regularization Of Sequential Minimal Optimization In Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
authors: Samuele Pedrielli, Frederik Stalschus, Stefan K\"uhn, Karl Jansen, Kim A. Nicoli, Shinichi Nakajima
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Nakanishi Fujii Todo (NFT) algorithm, also known as Rotosolve, implements Sequential Minimal Optimization for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (SMO-VQE) by exploiting the trigonometric dependence of the energy on individual circuit parameters. This enables analytical one-dimensional minimization using only a few , typically two, energy evaluations, but introduces bias in the estimated energy. Although performing additional measurements every few tens of iterations can mitigate bias accumulation, we find that such corrections often degrade optimization performance.
