conclusion: The method shows promise for extension to fast boundary integral equation solvers for large-scale electromagnetic problems, but is purely computational and not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Bounds On The Number Of Modes Of A Gaussian Mixture Density
authors: Hien Duy Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive explicit upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate critical points of a [MATH]-component Gaussian mixture density in [MATH], and the number of modes when the modal set is finite, together with lower bounds. By normalizing the critical-point equations by a reference component, for [MATH] we get the direct Pfaffian bound \[ U_{}(d,k)=2^{\,d+{2}}\left(d+2\min(d,k-1)+1\right)^{k-1}. \] For the same parameter range, an exact elimination augmented by an algebraic reciprocal variable gives the alternative bound \[ U_{}(d,k)= 2^{{2}}(d+1)\left((2k-1)d+2k-1\right)^{k-1}. \] Thus, for [MATH], the best critical-point bound is their minimum. A Morse-theoretic argument improves the corresponding finite-mode upper bound to \[ \left\lfloor }(d,k),U_{}(d,k)\}+1}{2}\right\rfloor. \] In the homoscedastic case, for [MATH], the direct bound improves to \[ U_{}(d,k)=2^{\,d+{2}}\left(d+\min(d,k-1)+1\right)^{k-1}, \] an affine-rank reduction replaces [MATH] by the affine rank of the component means, and an augmented homoscedastic reduction gives the dimension-free bound \[ U_{}(k)=2^{{2}+1}(2k)^{k-1}. \] On the lower-bound side, for [MATH] we obtain \[ L_{}(d,k)=k+\max_{2\le r\le \min(d,k)}{r}, \] together with a padding-product family that in particular implies the linear lower bound [MATH], and a seed-closure principle that packages product and padding constructions. We further give explicit bounds for the number of connected components of the critical set.
tldr: This paper derives upper and lower bounds on the number of modes (nondegenerate critical points) of Gaussian mixture densities in d dimensions with k components.
motivation: Understanding the number of modes in Gaussian mixtures is important for clustering and density estimation, but the paper is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests.
method: The authors use algebraic elimination, Pfaffian bounds, Morse theory, and affine-rank reduction to derive bounds on critical points and modes.
result: They provide explicit upper bounds (e.g., U(d,k) = 2^{d+2}(d+2 min(d,k-1)+1)^{k-1}) and lower bounds (e.g., L(d,k) = k + max_{2≤r≤min(d,k)} r) for the number of modes.
conclusion: The bounds improve on previous results and are dimension-free in the homoscedastic case, but the work is theoretical and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Distributionally Robust Nash Equilibrium Seeking With Partial Observations And Distributed Communication
authors: Sonia Mart\'inez Nirabhra Mandal
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study stochastic one-shot games where agents' utilities depend on the collective strategy profiles of other agents as well as on some well-behaved randomness. While each decision-maker is agnostic to the random variable's underlying distribution, they have access to finitely many i.i.d. samples generated from it. We consider two cases: one where samples are shared; and another, more special one, where samples are individually accessible. To hedge against the unknown uncertainty, each agent plays a distributionally robust game and aims to maximize the worst-case expected utility over a Wasserstein ball around the sample average distribution. In this setting, we provide conditions under which the game has a non-empty set of distributionally robust Nash equilibria (DRoNE) and then characterize the closeness of the DRoNE set to the Nash equilibria (NE) of the associated stochastic game. We then propose an inertial, supported, better response, ascending supergradient dynamics ISBRAG that seeks the DRoNE's when the distributionally robust game possesses what we term as amicable supergradients. This forms the basis of a distributed version (d-ISBRAG) where agents estimate others' strategies by means of a dynamic consensus subroutine over a directed communication network. While initially the distributed algorithm works in the case where agents have individual samples, we later extend this to the case of shared observations under certain simplifying assumptions. This involves analyzing a tractable reformulation of the distributionally robust optimization problem and solving it in a distributed manner to compute the required supergradients. Simulations illustrate our results.
tldr: This paper studies distributionally robust Nash equilibrium seeking in stochastic games with partial observations and distributed communication, using a Wasserstein ball ambiguity set and an inertial supergradient dynamics algorithm.
motivation: To address decision-making under uncertainty when agents have only finite samples of the random variable's distribution, and to develop distributed algorithms for equilibrium seeking in networked settings.
method: The authors formulate a distributionally robust game where each agent maximizes worst-case expected utility over a Wasserstein ball around the empirical distribution. They propose an inertial supported better response ascending supergradient dynamics (ISBRAG) and its distributed version (d-ISBRAG) with a dynamic consensus subroutine for estimating others' strategies over a directed communication network.
result: Conditions for existence of distributionally robust Nash equilibria (DRoNE) are provided, and the closeness of DRoNE to Nash equilibria of the stochastic game is characterized. The distributed algorithm converges under amicable supergradients.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for distributionally robust game theory with partial information and distributed computation, with potential applications in multi-agent systems under uncertainty.

title: A Weyl-type Theorem For Diophantine Approximations Driven By Lca Groups And Applications
authors: Aihua Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate actions of locally compact Abelian (LCA) groups on the torus [MATH], motivated by their close connection with Diophantine approximation. While Kronecker's theorem yields a classical density result, we prove a stronger equidistribution theorem of Weyl type: every such action admits a decomposition into uniquely ergodic subsystems. The proof of this result is based on a characterization of unique ergodicity for actions of amenable groups on compact metric spaces. As consequences, we establish several foundational results for LCA groups, including the Bohr orthogonality of characters along arbitrary Folner sequences, a Bohr mean formula for almost periodic functions, and a Wiener-type theorem on LCA groups characterizing the discrete part of a Borel probability measure through its Fourier transform.
tldr: This paper proves a Weyl-type equidistribution theorem for actions of locally compact Abelian groups on the torus, with applications to Diophantine approximation and harmonic analysis.
motivation: To extend classical equidistribution results (Kronecker, Weyl) to actions of general LCA groups, motivated by connections to Diophantine approximation.
method: Uses ergodic theory for amenable group actions on compact metric spaces, characterizing unique ergodicity and decomposing actions into uniquely ergodic subsystems.
result: Proves that every LCA group action on the torus admits a decomposition into uniquely ergodic subsystems; derives Bohr orthogonality, a Bohr mean formula, and a Wiener-type theorem for LCA groups.
conclusion: Provides foundational results for LCA groups with potential applications in number theory and harmonic analysis, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Decomposition And Successive Decomposition Methods And Algorithms For Nonconvex Optimization
authors: Yiqing Zhai, Ying Cui, Danny H. K. Tsang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing results on decomposition methods and algorithms for nonconvex problems are minimal. Parallel decomposition algorithms do not exist for nonconvex problems with coupling nonlinear equality constraints. Besides, decomposition structures (i.e., coupling variables and constraints) are not fully exploited in designing decomposition methods and algorithms. In this paper, we consider nonconvex problems with decomposition structures that are more general than those handled in the existing literature. We propose primal and dual decomposition and successive primal and successive dual decomposition methods and algorithms for these nonconvex problems, which exploit decomposition structures, allow for parallel and distributed implementations, produce the original nonconvex problems' stationary points, and offer good opportunities to achieve superior tradeoff between convergence performance and computation time. Finally, we compare the proposed methods and algorithms, extend them to indirect and two-level decomposition methods and algorithms, and provide examples and numerical results to demonstrate their respective values. Notably, the proposed decomposition and successive decomposition methods and algorithms generalize the basic ones for convex problems, and the proposed successive decomposition methods and algorithms extend the existing ones for nonconvex problems, together enriching the decomposition theory.
tldr: This paper proposes decomposition methods for nonconvex optimization problems, which are unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing decomposition methods for nonconvex problems are limited, especially for problems with coupling nonlinear equality constraints.
method: The authors develop primal and dual decomposition algorithms, including successive variants, that exploit decomposition structures and allow parallel/distributed implementation.
result: The proposed methods can find stationary points of nonconvex problems and offer tradeoffs between convergence and computation time.
conclusion: The methods generalize convex decomposition techniques and extend existing nonconvex approaches, enriching decomposition theory.

title: Travel-time Tomography From Mean Field Game Dynamics
authors: Longqiang Xu, Weishi Yin, Hongyu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Travel-time tomography seeks to recover a hidden environment from external measurements generated by propagation through an anomalous region. Standard formulations treat propagation as passive, so the environment influences observations mainly by bending paths or changing travel times. Many collective systems do not operate in that regime: observed arrivals are shaped by strategic motion, congestion, and environmental costs. We formulate this active setting through mean field games, in which the unknown environment enters the running cost through a spatial cost field and observations are read from the resulting population dynamics. This yields three contributions. First, it places propagation, observation generation, and inversion within one PDE-constrained model. Second, it clarifies why the inverse problem differs structurally from passive tomography: kinetic, congestion, and environmental effects are coupled endogenously and appear through space- and time-dependent local weights rather than externally chosen global coefficients. Third, it introduces a two-stage inversion pipeline that combines diffusion-based initialization with full mean field game refinement, and numerical experiments show stable recovery under noise and across multichannel scene families. Taken together, these ingredients establish a foundational framework for a class of inverse problems in which data are generated by optimizing and interacting populations rather than by passive signals. The framework identifies the forward MFG model, admissible observation channels, structural mechanisms, and computational recovery route needed to study active tomography under collective dynamics. Such problems arise, among other settings, in biological transport, vascular flow, and subsurface groundwater dynamics.
tldr: This paper introduces a travel-time tomography framework based on mean field game dynamics, where the environment is recovered from observations of strategic population motion rather than passive signal propagation.
motivation: Standard travel-time tomography assumes passive propagation, but many collective systems (e.g., biological transport, vascular flow) involve active, strategic motion. The authors aim to model and invert such active settings.
method: They formulate the forward problem as a mean field game (MFG) where the unknown environment appears in the running cost, and observations are derived from population dynamics. Inversion is performed via a two-stage pipeline: diffusion-based initialization followed by MFG refinement.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate stable recovery under noise and across multichannel scene families, showing that the MFG-based inversion captures coupled kinetic, congestion, and environmental effects.
conclusion: This establishes a foundational framework for active tomography problems where data are generated by optimizing and interacting populations, with potential applications in biological and geophysical systems.

title: Statistical Two-round Search For One Excellent Element
authors: Jong Sung Kim Nagananda K G
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and study a statistical version of Katona's two-round search problem of finding at least one excellent element in a set. A population of [MATH] elements is considered, where each element is independently excellent with probability [MATH], [MATH]. A subset test is noiseless: it returns positive exactly when the queried subset contains at least one excellent element. The goal is to minimize the expected number of tests subject to finding one excellent element with probability at least [MATH], where [MATH], under the restriction that testing is performed in two rounds. Unlike classical group testing, the objective is not to recover the full set of excellent elements, but only to identify one of them. We first show that success is fundamentally limited by the possibility that no excellent element exists. In the sparse Poisson regime, this imposes the necessary feasibility condition [MATH]. When the target success probability is feasible, we prove that the optimal expected number of tests grows logarithmically with the population size. The upper bound is obtained by combining an initial existence test with a second-round separating design; the lower bound follows from an information-counting argument. Numerical illustrations show the feasibility boundary and the resulting logarithmic scaling.
tldr: This paper studies a statistical two-round search problem to find one excellent element in a set using noiseless subset tests, with optimal expected number of tests scaling logarithmically.
motivation: To extend Katona's two-round search problem to a statistical setting where elements are excellent with a given probability, and to minimize expected tests under a success probability constraint.
method: Combines an initial existence test with a second-round separating design for the upper bound, and uses an information-counting argument for the lower bound.
result: The optimal expected number of tests grows logarithmically with population size when the target success probability is feasible, with a necessary feasibility condition in the sparse Poisson regime.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits and optimal strategies for statistical two-round search, with potential applications in group testing and search problems.

title: Optimal Harvesting Of A Stochastic Logistic Model Driven By One-Sided Tempered Stable Process
authors: Fu Zhang Wenmin Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a class of stochastic Logistic harvesting models driven by tempered stable processes, with a one-sided power-law L\'evy measure. We establish threshold conditions for population extinction and persistence, prove the distributional stability of the model, and derive explicit solutions for the optimal harvesting effort and the maximum sustainable yield. We systematically analyze the effects of white noise intensity and L\'evy jump intensity on the optimal harvesting strategy. In particular, by focusing on the intrinsic structural parameters of the L\'evy measure, namely the stability index and the tempering parameter, we elucidate their roles in shaping the optimal strategy and propose four targeted intervention strategies. Numerical simulations are presented to validate the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper studies optimal harvesting in a stochastic logistic model driven by tempered stable processes, focusing on population dynamics and sustainable yield.
motivation: To understand how heavy-tailed Lévy noise affects population extinction, persistence, and optimal harvesting strategies in ecological models.
method: The authors analyze a stochastic differential equation with a one-sided tempered stable process, derive threshold conditions, and solve for optimal harvesting effort using stochastic control theory.
result: Threshold conditions for extinction vs. persistence are established; explicit formulas for optimal harvesting effort and maximum sustainable yield are derived, showing dependence on white noise intensity, Lévy jump intensity, stability index, and tempering parameter.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights and intervention strategies for managing populations under heavy-tailed noise, with potential applications in ecology and resource management.

title: Rigorous Construction Of Stop-and-Go Waves In The Optimal Velocity Model Via A Difference-Differential Equation
authors: Tomoyuki Miyaji Kota Ikeda
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear wave phenomena such as stop-and-go traffic patterns are widely observed in vehicular flow but remain challenging to describe within a rigorous mathematical framework. Motivated by this, we investigate nonlinear wave structures in the optimal velocity (OV) model, which is a fundamental microscopic traffic flow model describing the car-following dynamics on a circuit. Using a traveling-wave formulation for vehicle headways, we reduce the original ordinary differential system to a difference-differential equation. We focus on steep OV functions approaching a step function, which generate sharp transition layers in the headway profile. In the singular limit, we explicitly construct heteroclinic transition layer solutions connecting two uniform traffic states. Motivated by related solvable queueing models in the literature, we rigorously prove the existence of heteroclinic traveling waves for sufficiently steep OV functions. We further establish the existence of homoclinic solutions arising from the interaction of increasing and decreasing transition layers, and derive a necessary condition for the amplitude parameter for their existence. To construct periodic stop-and-go waves on a circuit, we impose a global constraint reflecting the conservation of the total road length. Within this constrained framework, we prove the existence of large-period periodic solutions comprising alternating transition layers and quasi-uniform states. Beyond local bifurcation analysis, these results establish a rigorous foundation for nonlinear congestion waves. Furthermore, they contribute to the validation of car-following models and the design of control strategies to mitigate congestion.
tldr: This paper rigorously constructs stop-and-go wave solutions in the optimal velocity model for traffic flow using difference-differential equations.
motivation: Stop-and-go traffic patterns are common but lack rigorous mathematical description; the authors aim to provide a solid foundation for nonlinear congestion waves.
method: They reduce the OV model to a difference-differential equation via traveling-wave formulation, analyze steep OV functions approaching step functions, and use singular limit analysis to construct heteroclinic and homoclinic solutions.
result: Existence of heteroclinic traveling waves for steep OV functions is proved, homoclinic solutions from interacting layers are established, and large-period periodic solutions on a circuit are shown under a global constraint.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for nonlinear congestion waves, validating car-following models and aiding control strategy design.

title: A Tearing And Interconnecting Formulation For Magneto-Quasi-Statics
authors: Clemens Pechstein
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note deals with a tearing and interconnecting (special non-overlapping domain decomposition) formulation for magneto-quasi-statics (also known as the eddy current model). Only two subdomains are considered, one conducting and one insulating. Using a straightforward tree-cotree splitting, one can get rid of some kernel components in the non-conducting region, but due to the coupling across the interface, a lot of kernel functions remain that are associated with the interface. The formulation presented here overcomes this problem by using a space splitting into gradient fields and a complementary space. Under a mild condition on that splitting, it is shown that (i) one does not need any gradient part in the non-conducting domain, and therefore no coupling of any gradient components between the two subdomains, (ii) both subdomain operators are invertible, and (iii) although the magnetic vector potential is discontinuous across the subdomain interface, the corresponding magnetic field is globally in H(div).
tldr: This paper presents a domain decomposition formulation for magneto-quasi-statics (eddy current model) using a tree-cotree splitting to handle kernel components.
motivation: To overcome kernel function issues in non-overlapping domain decomposition for eddy current problems, particularly those associated with the interface between conducting and insulating subdomains.
method: A tearing and interconnecting formulation with a space splitting into gradient fields and a complementary space, combined with tree-cotree splitting.
result: Under a mild condition, gradient parts in the non-conducting domain are unnecessary, subdomain operators become invertible, and the magnetic field remains globally in H(div) despite discontinuous vector potential.
conclusion: The formulation provides a robust domain decomposition method for eddy current simulations, with potential extensions to more subdomains.

title: Viscosity-Informed Generative Actor-Critic For High-Dimensional Stochastic Optimal Control
authors: Alen E. Golpashin, Gokul Puthumanaillam, Melkior Ornik, Bruce A. Conway
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a method for approximating viscosity solutions of stationary degenerate elliptic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations on bounded domains arising in stochastic exit-time control. Viscosity enforcement is formulated as a min--max problem over an envelope-generated test family parameterized by symmetric positive definite matrices. Under structural and asymptotic assumptions, any uniform limit point of the value function approximations satisfies the viscosity inequalities on the sampled test family. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method reduces empirical viscosity violations and improves robustness under perturbed dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes a viscosity-informed generative actor-critic method for solving high-dimensional stochastic optimal control problems, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve the robustness and accuracy of solving degenerate elliptic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations in high-dimensional stochastic exit-time control problems.
method: Formulates viscosity enforcement as a min-max problem over an envelope-generated test family parameterized by symmetric positive definite matrices, and integrates it into a generative actor-critic framework.
result: Numerical experiments show reduced empirical viscosity violations and improved robustness under perturbed dynamics.
conclusion: The method offers a new way to enforce viscosity solutions in high-dimensional control, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect at best.

title: Optimum Peer-Turbo: A Scalable And Efficient Solution For P2p Broadcasting
authors: Muriel M\'edard, Kishori Konwar, Moritz Grundei, Vipindev Adat Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain systems such as Solana or Monad employ tree- or star-shaped broadcast topologies in which a single source node disseminates message shards to a set of target peers within a strictly bounded time window. In these architectures, shard propagation must complete before the next consensus step, making timely delivery to a large fraction of the validator set essential. A fundamental limitation of such designs is that the outbound bandwidth of the source node constitutes the primary system bottleneck. In this paper, we introduce peer Turbo, a technique that allows target nodes to exchange shards using Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC), thereby assisting each other in completing decoding without requiring explicit shard state coordination. We use a tractable fluid approximation of the degree of freedom distribution of peer-Turbo-enabled systems show that this approach reduces source bandwidth required for a set service quality by up to one order of magnitude, or equivalently reduces propagation latency by one order of magnitude under fixed bandwidth constraints.
tldr: This paper proposes a peer-to-peer broadcasting technique using Random Linear Network Coding to reduce source bandwidth and latency in blockchain systems.
motivation: To overcome the bottleneck of source node outbound bandwidth in tree- or star-shaped broadcast topologies used in blockchain consensus.
method: Introduces peer Turbo, where target nodes exchange shards using RLNC without explicit coordination, and uses a fluid approximation to analyze degree-of-freedom distribution.
result: Reduces required source bandwidth by up to an order of magnitude, or equivalently reduces propagation latency by an order of magnitude under fixed bandwidth.
conclusion: The technique offers scalable and efficient broadcasting for blockchain systems, with potential applications in other P2P networks.

title: Real-Time Reconstruction And Actuation Error Analysis For Markov Sources Over Mpr Channels
authors: Nikolaos Pappas Pansee S. Elessawy
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study real-time reconstruction and actuation for two binary Markov sources that share a wireless multi-packet reception (MPR) channel. Each sensor follows a stationary randomized sampling policy, and the receiver maintains source estimates using the most recently decoded updates. We derive closed-form expressions for the steady-state real-time reconstruction error (RTE) and the cost of actuation error (CAE) as functions of the source transition probabilities and the effective update probabilities. We then characterize these update probabilities under randomized sampling, linking the physical-layer MPR model to task-oriented reconstruction and actuation metrics. Using these expressions, we formulate a sampling-constrained optimization problem with a weighted-error objective. The resulting analysis reveals how source dynamics, semantic weights, and MPR coupling affect the allocation of sampling resources. Numerical results show that optimized randomized sampling outperforms random, greedy, and time-sharing baselines.
tldr: This paper analyzes real-time reconstruction and actuation error for binary Markov sources over multi-packet reception channels, focusing on sampling optimization.
motivation: To optimize sampling policies for wireless sensors monitoring Markov sources, minimizing reconstruction and actuation errors under channel constraints.
method: Closed-form expressions for steady-state errors are derived as functions of source dynamics and effective update probabilities, linking physical-layer MPR model to task-oriented metrics; a sampling-constrained optimization problem is formulated.
result: Optimized randomized sampling outperforms random, greedy, and time-sharing baselines in minimizing weighted error objectives.
conclusion: The analysis provides insights into resource allocation for real-time monitoring over MPR channels, with potential extensions to more complex source models.

title: Degree Bounds For Positivstellens\"atze Of General Semialgebraic Sets
authors: Olga Heijmans-Kuryatnikova, Juan C. Vera, Luis F. Zuluaga
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] denote the minimum of a polynomial [MATH] over a (general) compact semialgebraic set [MATH]. A standard way to approximate [MATH] is via hierarchies built from Positivstellens\"atze, which certify nonnegativity of polynomials on [MATH] using sums of squares or other classes of globally nonnegative polynomials. As the degree of the certificate grows, the values generated by these hierarchies converge asymptotically to [MATH]. A natural question is, then, to determine explicit bounds on the certificate's degree needed to obtain a prescribed [MATH]-approximation to [MATH], or equivalently certify the positivity of [MATH] on [MATH]. We improve the current best degree bounds for Putinar's and Schm\"udgen's SOS-Positivstellensatz over [MATH]. Also, we obtain degree bounds for Krivine--Stengle's and the recently introduced extended-Handelman's [MATH]-Positivstellens\"atze over [MATH]; providing the first explicit degree bounds for linear optimization-based hierarchies over general compact semialgebraic sets. Our approach is based on a lift-and-project construction in which we add new variables to construct an algebraic representation of the distance to the set [MATH] using {\L}ojasiewicz's inequality. This lets us lift the problem of certifying the positivity of [MATH] on the (complex) set [MATH] to the problem of certifying the positivity of a related polynomial [MATH] on a higher-dimensional hypercube. By projecting out the added variables, non-negativity certificates for [MATH] on the hypercube become non-negativity certificates for [MATH] on [MATH]. Our approach offers a unified methodology to obtain degree bounds for several Positivstellensatz-based hierarchies over general compact sets, narrowing the gap between results for the hypercube (or other simple sets) and more general semialgebraic sets.
tldr: This paper improves degree bounds for Positivstellensätze to certify polynomial positivity on compact semialgebraic sets using a lift-and-project method.
motivation: To provide explicit degree bounds for polynomial optimization hierarchies over general compact semialgebraic sets, which were previously only known for simple sets like hypercubes.
method: The authors use a lift-and-project construction adding new variables to represent the distance to the set via Łojasiewicz's inequality, then lift positivity certification on the original set to a hypercube and project back.
result: Improved degree bounds for Putinar's and Schmüdgen's SOS-Positivstellensatz, and first explicit bounds for Krivine-Stengle's and extended-Handelman's Positivstellensätze over general compact semialgebraic sets.
conclusion: The unified approach narrows the gap between degree bounds for simple and general semialgebraic sets, advancing polynomial optimization theory.

title: Endpoint-singularity-preserving Spectral Approximation Theory For Weakly Singular Integral Equations
authors: Mahmoud A. Zaky
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a fractional approximation framework for functions with limited regularity near the terminal point. The proposed basis is constructed by composing classical Jacobi polynomials with an endpoint algebraic mapping, thereby incorporating the terminal singular structure directly into the approximation space. The main structural properties of the fractional polynomials are established, including orthogonality relations, derivative identities, and a singular Sturm--Liouville eigenvalue formulation. We then introduce the associated weighted Sobolev spaces and prove projection and Gauss-type interpolation error estimates in weighted norms. Inverse inequalities and weighted Sobolev embedding estimates are also derived. The resulting theory provides a rigorous foundation for high-order spectral and collocation approximations of endpoint-singular and weakly regular problems, including terminal value problems, fractional differential equations, and weakly singular Volterra integral equations.
tldr: This paper develops a spectral approximation framework for functions with endpoint singularities, using mapped Jacobi polynomials to solve weakly singular integral equations.
motivation: Standard spectral methods fail for functions with limited regularity near endpoints, which are common in fractional differential equations and weakly singular integral equations.
method: The authors construct a basis by composing classical Jacobi polynomials with an endpoint algebraic mapping, establishing orthogonality, derivative identities, and a singular Sturm-Liouville problem. They then derive error estimates in weighted Sobolev spaces.
result: The fractional polynomial basis preserves endpoint singularities and yields high-order convergence for weakly singular problems, with proven projection and interpolation error bounds.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous foundation for spectral and collocation methods for endpoint-singular problems, with potential applications in fractional calculus and integral equations.

title: Finding Directional Stationary Points Of Dc Programs
authors: Hoai An Le Thi, van Ngai Huynh, Tao Pham Dinh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the problem of computing stationary points for non-smooth, non-convex optimization problems. While this topic is well studied in the smooth setting, fewer algorithmic and theoretical results exist for the non-smooth case. Within Difference-of-Convex functions (DC) programming, the well-known DC Algorithm (DCA) is a standard method for computing critical points, whose definition depends on the chosen DC decomposition. More recently, some works have focused on computing directional stationary points - a stronger notion that does not depend on any particular DC decomposition - for specific non-smooth DC programs, where the second DC component is the pointwise maximum of finitely many smooth convex functions. In this contribution, we propose a new and unified approach for identifying directional stationary points of non-smooth DC programs, where both DC components may be non-smooth. Our framework generalizes both the classical DCA and the above recent approaches. It applies when the second DC component is the pointwise maximum of a continuous family of smooth convex functions, and more generally, to any continuous convex function on the whole space. We also establish strong convergence results. Specifically, when the second DC component is the pointwise maximum of finitely many [MATH] - smooth convex functions, we prove under the \L ojasiewicz inequality that the entire sequence generated by our algorithm converges. This extends previous results requiring global [MATH] - smoothness. Finally, we introduce a randomized (stochastic) variant of our method and prove its almost sure convergence, thereby extending our deterministic results to the randomized setting.
tldr: This paper proposes a new algorithm for finding directional stationary points in non-smooth DC programs, extending classical DCA and proving convergence under Lojasiewicz inequality.
motivation: To address the lack of algorithmic and theoretical results for computing stationary points in non-smooth, non-convex optimization, specifically directional stationary points which are stronger than critical points.
method: The authors develop a unified framework that generalizes DCA and recent approaches, applicable when the second DC component is a pointwise maximum of smooth convex functions or any continuous convex function. They also introduce a randomized variant.
result: Strong convergence results are established, including convergence of the entire sequence under Lojasiewicz inequality when the second component is a maximum of finitely many smooth convex functions, and almost sure convergence for the randomized variant.
conclusion: The work provides a more general and convergent method for non-smooth DC optimization, with implications for broader classes of problems, though not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: On Properties Of Normal Operators And Self-adjoint Operators On Smooth Banach Spaces
authors: Deepesh K P Mohammed Shameem
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article introduces classes of normal and unitary operators on smooth Banach spaces, providing extensions of the classical notions of normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to the smooth Banach space setting. The proposed class of normal operators contains, in particular, the class of self-adjoint operators on Banach spaces known in the literature. In addition, we study several properties of self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces, with emphasis on the norm, minimum modulus, numerical radius, and Crawford number, as well as the corresponding attainment properties and the relations among these quantities. Further, we obtain characterisations and spectral properties of the newly introduced classes of normal and unitary operators. Our results demonstrate close analogies with the corresponding theory of self-adjoint, normal, and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces.
tldr: This paper extends definitions of normal, unitary, and self-adjoint operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces, studying their properties and spectral characteristics.
motivation: To generalize fundamental operator classes beyond Hilbert spaces, which is a purely mathematical endeavor with no direct connection to the user's applied research interests.
method: The authors propose new definitions for normal and unitary operators on smooth Banach spaces using the duality mapping, then prove theorems about their properties, norms, numerical ranges, and spectra.
result: They show that the new classes contain existing self-adjoint operators on Banach spaces and exhibit analogies to Hilbert space theory, including characterizations and spectral properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to functional analysis but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems, making it irrelevant to the user's research.

title: Edge-indexed Network Time Series With Graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Dynamics
authors: Almut E. D. Veraart Jiaming Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a class of L\'evy-driven graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (grOU) models for edge-indexed network time series. The proposed framework extends generalized network autoregressive (GNAR) processes for edge-indexed network time series to continuous time and adapts graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, originally developed for node-indexed processes, to the edge-indexed setting. The model accommodates general L\'evy noise and therefore captures both Brownian and jump behavior. We show that the model parameters can be estimated via a maximum-likelihood framework and derive the asymptotic properties of the estimator. We examine the finite-sample performance of the methodology through simulation studies and illustrate its practical relevance in an empirical application to high-frequency financial data. The results indicate that grOU models for edge-indexed network time series improve forecasting accuracy and reduce computational time relative to standard benchmarks while maintaining robustness through their network-based parametrization.
tldr: This paper introduces a Lévy-driven graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model for edge-indexed network time series, focusing on financial data forecasting.
motivation: To extend network time series models to continuous time and edge-indexed settings, capturing both Brownian and jump behavior.
method: Extends generalized network autoregressive (GNAR) processes to continuous time using graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics with Lévy noise; parameters estimated via maximum likelihood.
result: The model improves forecasting accuracy and reduces computational time compared to standard benchmarks in high-frequency financial data.
conclusion: The grOU model offers a robust network-based parametrization for edge-indexed time series, with potential applications in finance and other fields.

title: Restricted Quantum Groups As Graded Hopf Algebras
authors: Giovanni Felder Jelena Ani\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of [MATH]-graded Hopf algebra, where the grading is by the double groupoid of commutative diagrams of a finite groupoid [MATH]. The finite dimensional representations of a [MATH]-graded Hopf algebra form a rigid monoidal category with a fibre functor to the category of [MATH]-graded vector spaces. The main example is given by the restricted quantum groups underlying the Andrews-Baxter-Forrester restricted solid-on-solid models of statistical mechanics and, more generally, the Jimbo-Miwa-Okado models associated to classical Lie algebras.
tldr: The paper introduces graded Hopf algebras based on double groupoids of finite groupoids, with restricted quantum groups as examples, but does not connect to the user's research interests.
motivation: To develop a mathematical framework for graded Hopf algebras that generalizes existing structures and applies to statistical mechanics models.
method: The authors define [MATH]-graded Hopf algebras using double groupoids and study their representation theory, showing that finite-dimensional representations form a rigid monoidal category with a fiber functor.
result: The main example is restricted quantum groups underlying the Andrews-Baxter-Forrester and Jimbo-Miwa-Okado models.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic structure but is purely mathematical with no direct implications for the user's research areas.

title: Delay Periodic Lyapunov Equation
authors: Juan J. L. Vel\'azquez Irina V. Aleksandrova
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For linear periodic finite-dimensional systems, it is well-known that, first, exponential stability is equivalent to the existence of a unique periodic positive definite solution to the Lyapunov equation, and second, the Lyapunov equation admits a unique periodic solution, if and only if the monodromy matrix has no reciprocal eigenvalues. In the present paper, we generalize these results to the case of periodic evolution families on a Hilbert space, with application to the stability theory of linear periodic systems with constant delays. More precisely, we first link the existence and uniqueness of a quadratic periodic Lyapunov functional with the existence and uniqueness of the solution to a discrete operator Lyapunov equation with the monodromy operator involved. Second, we show that the presented theory on a Hilbert space gives rise to an alternative definition of the delay Lyapunov matrix, the concept previously appeared in the construction of quadratic Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals for a class of linear periodic delay systems. An explicit connection between the infinite-dimensional Hilbert setting and the previously developed delay Lyapunov matrix framework is established. An important consequence is the uniqueness theorem: the delay Lyapunov matrix exists and is unique, if and only if the monodromy operator has no reciprocal eigenvalues. As a by-product, our framework enables the construction of Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals for periodic delay systems without a preliminary exponential stability assumption as in earlier theory.
tldr: This paper generalizes Lyapunov equation theory to periodic delay systems on Hilbert spaces, establishing existence and uniqueness conditions for delay Lyapunov matrices.
motivation: To extend classical Lyapunov stability theory for periodic systems to those with constant delays, which is important for control theory but not directly related to the user's interests.
method: The authors use operator theory on Hilbert spaces, linking periodic evolution families to discrete operator Lyapunov equations involving the monodromy operator.
result: They prove that a unique delay Lyapunov matrix exists iff the monodromy operator has no reciprocal eigenvalues, and they connect this to quadratic Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for stability analysis of periodic delay systems, but its applications are in control theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kolmogorov Invariant Torus Theorem For Weakly Interacting Particles I: Full Dimensional Tori
authors: Dmitry Dolgopyat, Bassam Fayad, Jaime Paradela
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an abstract KAM theorem for systems of infinitely many interacting particles with decaying masses and all-to-all interactions. Using this framework, we construct full-dimensional KAM tori for infinite-dimensional mechanical systems exhibiting long range interactions.
tldr: This paper proves a KAM theorem for infinite-dimensional systems with long-range interactions, constructing full-dimensional tori.
motivation: To extend KAM theory to systems with infinitely many particles and all-to-all interactions, which are common in statistical mechanics and field theory.
method: Develops an abstract KAM framework that handles decaying masses and long-range interactions, then applies it to construct invariant tori.
result: Full-dimensional KAM tori exist for infinite-dimensional mechanical systems with long-range interactions under certain conditions.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous foundation for quasiperiodic motion in infinite particle systems, with potential applications to statistical mechanics and nonlinear dynamics.

title: Node-private Community Estimation In Stochastic Block Models: Tractable Algorithms And Lower Bounds
authors: Laurentiu Marchis, Ethan D'souza, Tom\'a\v{s} Fl\'idr, Po-Ling Loh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classical problem of community recovery in stochastic block models with a fixed number of communities, with a twist: We seek algorithms that are stable with respect to node-wise changes in the graph structure, formally defined as a differential privacy constraint. The algorithms we develop are based on spectral clustering, where we introduce privacy to the community recovery pipeline in the form of directly privatizing the adjacency matrix; private PCA; private convex optimization; private low-rank matrix estimation; and private approximate subspace estimation. Straightforward applications of existing private algorithms lead to a rapid increase in the privacy parameter [MATH] in order to ensure consistent estimation under node differential privacy, in contrast with the simpler setting of edge privacy. To alleviate these issues, we develop novel algorithms based on (1) sampling from an exponential mechanism with a Lipschitz extension and (2) a general framework for constructing smooth projections from the space of undirected graphs to the space of bounded-degree graphs, which can then be combined with various edge-private algorithms. Importantly, the methods we develop are all computable in polynomial-time as a function of the number of nodes in the graph. We also develop novel lower bounds on the growth rate of [MATH] required in order to achieve consistent community estimation under node privacy. On a technical note, our paper highlights the complications that arise when analyzing private algorithms under the non-standard scaling [MATH] and proposes some solutions. We also provide a novel application of the HGR maximal correlation from information theory in the context of accuracy amplification in PAC learning, which may be of independent interest.
tldr: This paper studies node-private community estimation in stochastic block models, focusing on differential privacy and spectral clustering, with no direct connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: To develop algorithms for community recovery that are stable under node-wise changes in graph structure, formalized as node differential privacy.
method: Uses spectral clustering with privacy mechanisms including private PCA, convex optimization, low-rank matrix estimation, and approximate subspace estimation; also introduces an exponential mechanism with Lipschitz extension and a framework for smooth projections to bounded-degree graphs.
result: Novel algorithms achieve consistent community estimation under node privacy with polynomial-time computability, and lower bounds on the required privacy parameter are derived.
conclusion: The work highlights complications in private algorithms under non-standard scaling and provides a novel application of HGR maximal correlation for accuracy amplification in PAC learning.

title: Vectorized Generalized Nearest Neighbor Decoding For In-block Memory Channel
authors: Yuhao Liu, Xinwei Li, Shuqin Pang, Hao Wu, Wenyi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends the generalized nearest neighbor decoding (GNND), originally developed as a receiver architecture for memoryless channels, to a vectorized GNND (Vec-GNND) suitable for in-block memory (IBM) channels. Leveraging the generalized mutual information (GMI) as an operational lower bound on the mismatch capacity, an analytical characterization of the optimal Vec-GNND is obtained for general IBM channels with Gaussian codebooks. The formalism further provides closed-form optimality conditions and achievable GMIs for restricted variants of the receiver architecture. Furthermore, we formulate a GMI-based joint design viewpoint for Gaussian codebook covariance and decoding metrics. Since the metric optimization admits a closed-form solution for each fixed covariance, the joint design is reduced to an input-covariance optimization problem; for the diagonal covariance family, we derive first-order self-consistent optimality conditions. Numerical evaluations on block noncoherent additive white Gaussian noise channels and phase noise channels demonstrate consistent performance gains over conventional scaling-based baselines, highlighting the substantial advantages and potential relevance of the proposed Vec-GNND in realistic communication scenarios.
tldr: This paper extends generalized nearest neighbor decoding to vectorized form for in-block memory channels, optimizing decoding metrics via generalized mutual information.
motivation: To improve decoding performance in channels with memory, which are common in realistic communication systems, by extending a memoryless-channel receiver architecture.
method: The authors propose a vectorized generalized nearest neighbor decoding (Vec-GNND) and analytically characterize its optimality using generalized mutual information (GMI) with Gaussian codebooks, reducing joint design to covariance optimization.
result: Closed-form optimality conditions and achievable GMIs are derived; numerical evaluations on block noncoherent AWGN and phase noise channels show consistent gains over conventional baselines.
conclusion: Vec-GNND offers substantial advantages for in-block memory channels, with potential for practical implementation in realistic communication scenarios.

title: Copositive Matrices With Ordered Off-Diagonal Entries
authors: Grigoriy Blekherman, Santanu S. Dey, Alex Dunbar, Burak Kocuk
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study copositive matrices which admit a decomposition into a sum of a positive semidefinite matrix and a matrix with nonnegative entries. Our main result shows that if the off-diagonal entries of a copositive matrix are nondecreasing in rows and in columns, then it admits such a decomposition. We apply this result to study optimization of quadratic forms over the standard simplex. As a corollary, we obtain that a natural relaxation of this problem is tight when the objective function is separable, resolving an open question of Dey and Kocuk.
tldr: This paper studies copositive matrices with ordered off-diagonal entries and their decomposition into sum of a positive semidefinite matrix and a nonnegative matrix, with applications to quadratic optimization over the simplex.
motivation: To characterize when a copositive matrix admits a decomposition into a sum of a positive semidefinite matrix and a nonnegative matrix, and to resolve an open question about tightness of a relaxation for separable objective functions.
method: The authors prove a structural theorem using combinatorial and matrix analysis techniques, showing that if off-diagonal entries are nondecreasing in rows and columns, the decomposition exists. They then apply this to quadratic optimization over the simplex.
result: The main result is that copositive matrices with monotone off-diagonal entries admit the desired decomposition. As a corollary, a natural relaxation for quadratic optimization over the simplex is tight when the objective is separable.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into copositive matrices and optimization, but the results are primarily in combinatorial optimization and matrix theory, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Singular Control With State-dependent Costs For L\'evy Processes
authors: Mordecki Ernesto, Muler Nora, Oli\'u Facundo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a discounted singular stochastic control problem driven by a general L\'evy process, where the objective is to minimize a cost functional composed of a running cost and a control cost that depends on the current state of the process. We first establish a Hamilton Jacobi Bellman (HJB)-type verification theorem providing sufficient conditions under which a reflecting barrier strategy is optimal and characterizing the value function. Our main contribution is to connect this control problem with an associated optimal stopping problem: we prove that the optimal reflection threshold coincides with the optimal stopping boundary of the auxiliary problem. This connection allows us to characterize the optimal strategy through probabilistic tools and leads to explicit or semi-explicit solutions in several relevant cases. We illustrate the results with several examples, including an application to pollution abatement.
tldr: This paper studies a singular stochastic control problem for Lévy processes with state-dependent costs, linking it to an optimal stopping problem.
motivation: To understand optimal control strategies for systems driven by Lévy processes where control costs depend on the current state, with applications like pollution abatement.
method: Establishes a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman verification theorem and connects the control problem to an associated optimal stopping problem to characterize the optimal reflecting barrier strategy.
result: The optimal reflection threshold coincides with the optimal stopping boundary of the auxiliary problem, enabling explicit or semi-explicit solutions in several cases.
conclusion: Provides a probabilistic characterization of optimal strategies for singular control with state-dependent costs, with potential applications in environmental economics.

title: Enabling Adversarial Robustness In Ai Models Through Kubeflow MLOps
authors: Stavros Bouras, Ioannis Korontanis, Antonios Makris, Konstantinos Tserpes
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI models are increasingly deployed in cloud-native environments to support scalable and automated services. However, while platforms such as Kubernetes provide strong infrastructure orchestration, security mechanisms specifically designed to protect deployed AI models remain limited. This paper presents security measures for AI models deployed in Kubernetes clusters. The proposed architecture integrates Kubeflow-based MLOps to automatically detect adversarial attacks during the inference phase and trigger defense mechanisms that preserve the model's accuracy and reliability. Specifically, a Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) attack is applied at inference time, and a Projected Gradient Descent (PGD)-based adversarial training defense is automatically deployed when a degradation in accuracy is detected. The experimental results indicate that the deployed defense robustifies the model, significantly recovering accuracy relative to the degradation caused by the attack.
tldr: This paper presents a Kubeflow-based MLOps architecture to detect and defend against adversarial attacks (FGSM, PGD) on AI models deployed in Kubernetes, but it is unrelated to quantum computing or the user's specific research interests.
motivation: AI models deployed in cloud-native environments lack security mechanisms against adversarial attacks, motivating the need for automated detection and defense.
method: The authors integrate Kubeflow MLOps with Kubernetes to monitor inference accuracy, detect FGSM attacks, and trigger PGD-based adversarial training as a defense.
result: The defense mechanism significantly recovers model accuracy after an FGSM attack, demonstrating improved robustness.
conclusion: The work shows feasibility of automated adversarial defense in MLOps pipelines, but it is limited to classical machine learning and does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Distance-Preserving Digests: A Primitive For Bft Consensus
authors: Ryan Patrick Mercier
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every BFT consensus protocol uses collision-resistant hashes to compare validator state. Collision resistance destroys distance: two validators agreeing on 19 of 20 transactions produce unrelated hashes, indistinguishable from validators sharing nothing. This forces three design constraints across the BFT literature: validators must synchronize state before voting, agreement quality cannot be measured until votes are counted, and hierarchical committees must be large enough for independent BFT, limiting tree depth. This paper introduces distance-preserving transaction digests, a primitive that replaces collision-resistant hashes with commutative vector sums in 8-dimensional space. The primitive has three properties hashes lack: distance is proportional to disagreement, weighted means are exact, and set differences are identifiable via bloom filter diff. We demonstrate three applications: a two-phase BFT protocol (Proxima) that achieves single-round finality when validators agree; tree-structured consensus with groups of 10 validators (vs 128 in Ethereum), enabled because distance filtering replaces per-group BFT; and cross-shard consistency verification at 128 bytes per shard pair, replacing the per-transaction coordination of two-phase commit. Safety is proved: fewer than N/3 Byzantine validators cannot cause conflicting finalization, independent of Phase 1 clustering or tree topology. At N =100,000, Proxima Tree uses 2.2x fewer messages than HotStuff (a structural property unaffected by parallelism). Single-core finality is 0.9s vs 18s for HotStuff; multi-core BLS narrows but does not eliminate this gap.
tldr: This paper introduces distance-preserving digests for BFT consensus, replacing collision-resistant hashes with vector sums to enable disagreement measurement and efficient tree-structured consensus.
motivation: Existing BFT protocols rely on collision-resistant hashes that destroy distance information, forcing state synchronization before voting and limiting scalability. The authors aim to overcome these constraints.
method: The primitive uses commutative vector sums in 8-dimensional space to produce digests that preserve distance proportional to disagreement, support weighted means, and enable set difference identification via bloom filter diff.
result: Three applications are demonstrated: a two-phase BFT protocol (Proxima) with single-round finality under agreement, tree-structured consensus with groups of 10 validators, and cross-shard consistency verification at 128 bytes per shard pair. Safety is proved against < N/3 Byzantine validators.
conclusion: The approach significantly reduces message complexity and latency compared to HotStuff, enabling scalable BFT consensus. Future work may explore further optimizations and applications.

title: Learning To Persuade A Biased Receiver
authors: Yuqi Pan, Sadie Zhao, Milind Tambe, Yiling Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a repeated information design setting in which the receiver, who is also the decision-maker, updates beliefs in a systematically biased way. More specifically, a distorted posterior in our model can be written as a convex combination of the prior and the Bayesian posterior, governed by a fixed but unknown parameter. Over repeated interactions, the sender chooses persuasive signaling schemes, observes only the receiver's realized actions, and seeks to minimize regret relative to a full-information oracle that knows the receiver's biased updating rule. We propose a safe exploration algorithm for learning the receiver's bias while maintaining high persuasion value. The algorithm exploits the asymmetric cost of probing: conservative probes incur only local loss, whereas overly aggressive probes may lose the persuasive opportunity entirely. For general finite state and action spaces and arbitrary bounded utilities, our method achieves [MATH] regret. A matching [MATH] lower bound shows that this rate is optimal. We further discuss the influence on receiver welfare, as well as extensions to jointly unknown prior and bias, and contextual settings with time-varying priors and utilities.
tldr: This paper studies a repeated information design problem where a sender learns to persuade a receiver with a biased belief-updating rule, achieving optimal regret bounds.
motivation: To understand how a sender can optimally persuade a receiver whose belief updating deviates from Bayesian rationality, and to design algorithms that learn the bias while maintaining persuasion value.
method: The authors propose a safe exploration algorithm that exploits the asymmetric cost of probing, using regret analysis and lower bounds to characterize optimal performance.
result: The algorithm achieves O(√T) regret, matching a lower bound, and extends to settings with unknown prior and bias, as well as contextual environments.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for learning in information design with biased receivers, with implications for algorithmic persuasion and welfare analysis.

title: Interpreting De Finetti's Theorem In The Category Of Integrable Cones (long Version)
authors: Crubill\'e Rapha\"elle
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a connection between two results in the literature on probabilistic semantics: a formulation of De Finetti's theorem in the language of category theory due to Jacobs and Staton, and the generic construction of the free exponential of Linear Logic by Melli\`es et al, that has been instantiated in the model of probabilistic coherence spaces by Crubill\'e et al. The structural proximity of these two constructions is manifest, but making this connection formal requires technical developments on the relationship between the category of stochastic kernels and the category of integrable cones, two well-known categories in probabilistic semantics. We then use this connection to give a characterization of the total elements of the probabilistic coherence space !Bool.
tldr: This paper connects De Finetti's theorem in category theory with the free exponential of Linear Logic in probabilistic coherence spaces.
motivation: To formalize the structural proximity between two known constructions in probabilistic semantics.
method: Develops technical relationships between the category of stochastic kernels and the category of integrable cones.
result: Establishes a connection and uses it to characterize total elements of the probabilistic coherence space !Bool.
conclusion: Provides a deeper categorical understanding of probabilistic semantics, but is purely theoretical and not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Understanding Cdcl Solvers Via Scalability Studies And Proofdoors
authors: Shimin Zhang, Yechuan Xia, Chunxiao Li, Jianwen Li, Moshe Y. Vardi, Vijay Ganesh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over the past several decades, CDCL SAT solvers have proven remarkably effective on large industrial formulas, despite SAT being NP-complete and widely believed to be intractable. While considerable empirical research has been done on solver performance over benchmarks like the SAT competition, as well as scaling studies on random and crafted families, surprisingly little effort has gone into systematic scaling studies over industrial instances. To address this gap, we collect a large benchmark of Bounded Model Checking (BMC) instances (76,600+ across 766 families) and perform a systematic scaling study of solver performance. We observe a spectrum: some families scale linearly, others polynomially or exponentially. Building on this foundation, we study the structural parameters that have been proposed to explain this phenomenon. We first show that previously proposed parameters -- clause-variable ratio, treewidth, and community structure -- fail to discriminate between the linear and exponential regimes. By contrast, the recently proposed parameter explains this phenomenon well. Informally, a proofdoor is a sequence of interpolants between chunks of a formula, where each interpolant represents the solver's memoization of reasoning effort on chunks it has already analyzed. In support of the proofdoor hypothesis, we make three key contributions. First, we empirically show that CDCL solvers do compute small proofdoors for linearly-scaling BMC instances. Second, we show that for exponentially-scaling instances, sampled proofdoors scale exponentially and are typically not incrementally absorbed. Third, we show that scrambling linearly-scaling instances yields larger proofdoor sizes relative to pre-scrambling, relating poor branching order to larger proofdoor sizes and drop in solver performance.
tldr: This paper studies scalability of CDCL SAT solvers on industrial BMC instances and introduces the concept of proofdoors to explain performance differences.
motivation: Despite the success of CDCL solvers, there is a lack of systematic scaling studies on industrial instances; the authors aim to understand why some instances scale linearly while others scale exponentially.
method: The authors collect a large benchmark of BMC instances (76,600+ across 766 families) and perform scaling studies. They analyze structural parameters like clause-variable ratio, treewidth, community structure, and the newly proposed proofdoor parameter.
result: Previously proposed parameters fail to discriminate between linear and exponential scaling, but proofdoor size correlates well: linearly-scaling instances have small proofdoors, while exponentially-scaling ones have large proofdoors that are not incrementally absorbed.
conclusion: The proofdoor hypothesis provides a plausible explanation for CDCL solver performance on industrial instances, suggesting that solver efficiency depends on the ability to memoize reasoning via interpolants.

title: Coalgebraic Non-Wellfounded Proofs: Recursiveness And Gtc
authors: Mayuko Kori
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-wellfounded proof systems impose a global condition called the global trace condition (GTC) on a derivation tree to ensure soundness. Providing a categorical characterisation of the GTC that guarantees soundness remains challenging due to the global, non-compositional nature of these conditions and the infinitary structure of non-wellfounded proofs. We develop a coalgebraic framework for non-wellfounded proof systems where derivation trees are modelled as coalgebras of generalised polynomial functors on presheaves. Since the GTC is a constraint on infinite paths in derivation graphs, we employ graphs of coalgebras and formulate the GTC coalgebraically as a condition on these graphs. Soundness is then formulated as the existence of a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism from a coalgebra representing a derivation graph to an algebra specifying semantics. Within this framework, we characterise the GTC via recursive coalgebras: a coalgebra satisfies the GTC if and only if its image under a suitable adjoint is recursive. Under an appropriate assumption on the given semantic algebra, this yields soundness, that is, every proof admits a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism. We demonstrate our framework through a non-wellfounded proof system for the modal mu-calculus, one for higher-order fixed-point logics, and a non-wellfounded variant of Santocanale's circular proof system in mu-bicomplete categories.
tldr: This paper develops a coalgebraic framework for non-wellfounded proofs, focusing on the global trace condition and recursive coalgebras, with applications to modal mu-calculus and fixed-point logics.
motivation: To provide a categorical characterisation of the global trace condition (GTC) in non-wellfounded proof systems, which is challenging due to its global and non-compositional nature.
method: Models derivation trees as coalgebras of generalised polynomial functors on presheaves, uses graphs of coalgebras to formulate GTC, and characterises GTC via recursive coalgebras.
result: A coalgebra satisfies GTC iff its image under a suitable adjoint is recursive; under appropriate assumptions, this yields soundness (unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism).
conclusion: The framework is demonstrated on proof systems for modal mu-calculus, higher-order fixed-point logics, and a non-wellfounded variant of Santocanale's circular proof system, but the paper is purely theoretical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: The Privacy Subsidy: Kyle's $\lambda$ Under Noise-Perturbed Order-Flow Observation
authors: Yuki Nakamura
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-preserving cryptocurrency exchanges (shielded AMMs, batched swap auctions, sealed-bid order-flow auctions) alter what the pricing mechanism observes about order flow. We derive the unique linear Kyle equilibrium when a committed Bayesian market maker observes order flow perturbed by independent Gaussian privacy noise. The price-impact coefficient and informed-trader strategy both rescale by a single factor in the privacy parameter, and their product is invariant. A welfare decomposition then identifies a closed-form per-period transfer from the protocol's LP pool to traders -- the "privacy subsidy", the break-even fee any privacy-aggregated exchange must charge. The result is the single-period closed-form privacy-noise analog of Loss-Versus-Rebalancing (Milionis et al. 2022). The primary application is shielded AMMs with explicit additive-noise injection (e.g., differential privacy); related designs (batched swaps, sealed-bid auctions, oracle-pegged crossings) require separate frameworks that we leave to future work.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of privacy noise on order-flow observation in cryptocurrency exchanges, deriving a linear Kyle equilibrium and a 'privacy subsidy' analogous to Loss-Versus-Rebalancing.
motivation: To understand how privacy-preserving mechanisms in decentralized exchanges affect pricing, trader strategies, and welfare, and to quantify the necessary fees for such exchanges.
method: The author derives a unique linear Kyle equilibrium model where a Bayesian market maker observes order flow perturbed by independent Gaussian privacy noise, and performs a welfare decomposition.
result: The price-impact coefficient and informed-trader strategy rescale by a single factor in the privacy parameter, their product is invariant, and a closed-form per-period transfer (privacy subsidy) is identified.
conclusion: The results provide a closed-form analog of Loss-Versus-Rebalancing for privacy-aggregated exchanges, with primary application to shielded AMMs using differential privacy; other designs require separate frameworks.

title: An Enriched Model Of Strategic Voting Under Uncertainty
authors: S\'ebastien Destercke Henri Surugue
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new strategic voting model where we use uncertainty representation to model preferences. Specifically, we use probability sets as uncertainty representations, together with lower and upper expected utility gains to take strategic decisions. Focusing on belief functions in particular, we demonstrate that this very expressive model includes in one sweep many existing models based on probabilities, sets or incomplete preferences. Additionally, we generalize several well-known convergence results from the literature to this broader representational setting. Furthermore, we illustrate how this model can capture more realistic scenarios for practical applications but also raises theoretical challenges.
tldr: This paper proposes a strategic voting model using uncertainty representations like probability sets and belief functions, generalizing existing models and convergence results.
motivation: To develop a more expressive strategic voting model that can capture realistic preference uncertainty beyond traditional probabilistic or set-based approaches.
method: The authors use probability sets and lower/upper expected utility gains to model strategic decisions, focusing on belief functions as a specific uncertainty representation.
result: The model unifies many existing models (probabilistic, set-based, incomplete preferences) and generalizes several convergence results from the literature.
conclusion: The model can capture more realistic scenarios but raises theoretical challenges; it is primarily relevant to social choice and decision theory, not quantum information or physics.

title: FedEDAuth -- Federated Embedding Distribution Authentication For Counterfeit Ic Detection
authors: Naseeruddin Lodge, Dhruva Aklekar, Vineet Chadalavada, Nahush Tambe, Sina Gholami, Minhaj Alam, Fareena Saqib
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The widespread of counterfeit integrated circuits (ICs) poses severe risks to the security, reliability, and trustworthiness of modern electronic systems. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative counterfeit detection across the semiconductor supply chain, but its vulnerability to byzantine data poisoning attacks limits practical deployment. This paper presents Federated Embedding Distribution Authentication (FedEDAuth), a lightweight, embedding level client authentication framework that detects and filters malicious participants before model aggregation. FedEDAuth leverages reference embedding distributions derived from a golden dataset and evaluates clients using outlier analysis, mean shift measurements, and micro-cluster behavior without requiring access to raw data or gradients. Integrated into standard FL pipelines, FedEDAuth consistently identifies all poisoned clients in experimental settings with 50 distributed participants under the byzantine data poisoning attack, achieving a 100% malicious client detection rate. After filtering, the federated model achieved a high counterfeit IC classification performance of 94.17% accuracy. These results not only validate FedEDAuth's effectiveness but also underscore the broader potential of secure, trustworthy FL frameworks as a critical advancement for next generation hardware security solutions, enabling robust, collaborative intelligence across the semiconductor supply chain.
tldr: FedEDAuth is a federated learning authentication framework for detecting counterfeit ICs, focusing on security against data poisoning attacks.
motivation: Counterfeit ICs threaten electronic system security, and federated learning for detection is vulnerable to byzantine attacks.
method: FedEDAuth uses reference embedding distributions from a golden dataset and applies outlier analysis, mean shift, and micro-cluster behavior to authenticate clients without accessing raw data.
result: The method achieves 100% detection of malicious clients and 94.17% classification accuracy in experiments with 50 participants under poisoning attacks.
conclusion: FedEDAuth demonstrates a secure federated learning framework for hardware security, with potential for broader supply chain applications.

title: A Multi-Layer Cloud-IDS Pipeline With Llm And Adaptive Q-Learning Calibration
authors: Syed Waqas Ali, Ibrar Ali Shah, Farzana Zahid, Daniyal Munir, Hans D. Schotten
abstract: ArXiv:2605.15889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security in cloud computing has become a major concern due to several factors such as layered cloud architectures, dynamic environments, and exposure to unseen or zero-day attacks. Moreover, intrusion detection systems (IDS) typically operate at specific layers and rely heavily on machine learning models, which often perform well in experimental settings but fail to sustain performance in real cloud deployments. In this work, we implement a confidence-aware multilevel intrusion detection system using reinforcement learning tailored for cloud environments. The system secures three distinct layers: network, host, and hypervisor. Machine learning models at each layer detect known attack patterns, while prediction confidence distinguishes reliable decisions from uncertain outcomes. Within the multi-gate flow, low-confidence events pass through a learned-threshold confidence gate (Gate-1), followed by a Chroma memory-matching gate (Gate-2), with unresolved events escalated to a large language model (LLM) for semantic analysis and explanation. Final attack promotion at Gate-3 uses calibrated LLM confidence or weighted-fusion fallback, while uncertain events are retained in a review bucket to avoid forced classification. Generated explanations and confirmed knowledge are stored in ChromaDB to support future analysis and retraining. The approach is first evaluated using static thresholds, establishing a baseline for comparison. Results show that the proposed system learns adaptive thresholds and reduces LLM escalation by 58.78%, lowering cost while maintaining strong performance (88.68% accuracy, 85.29% precision, 84.72% recall, 85.00% F1). The network and hypervisor layers achieve 98.02% and 97.08% accuracy, demonstrating a balanced and efficient detection system.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-layer cloud intrusion detection system using reinforcement learning and LLMs, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or foundations.
motivation: Cloud security faces challenges from layered architectures and zero-day attacks; existing IDS often fail in real deployments.
